commits.message:
[CI][EPLB] Revert #17579 to diagnose Qwen3-235B PD decoder startup (#23274)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reverts #17579 on main `6e1ed5a7` to test whether the EPLB changes
contribute to the Qwen3-235B A3 PD decoder startup failure. In the
original run, decoder workers had EPLB enabled and failed during
piecewise graph capture. The device log reported an unresolved kernel
name in SuperKernel optimization. [Original failing
job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45572445719/job/139062848261)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Restores the previous EPLB map and record kernels and removes map warmup
registration introduced by #17579.

### How was this patch tested?

Verified the restored kernel file matches the parent of #17579 and ran
`git diff --check`. The target nightly case is
`QWEN3_235B_PD_3_5K_1_5k`. The original run used vLLM-Ascend `7dcdb690`;
this diagnostic PR uses a newer main baseline.
- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

Signed-off-by: AuroraEmiya <Sakura.iostream@gmail.com>

-# EPLB mapping and expert-load kernels
-
-## Description
-
-- **Function**: Model Runner V2 EPLB uses `map_to_physical_triton` from the Ascend MoE router to map logical expert IDs to physical IDs. The EPLB layer state calls `record_expert_tokens_triton` after MoE execution to accumulate local expert counts.
-- **Formula**:
-    - Mapping: `physical_ids[t,j] = routing_table[t % R, topk_ids[t,j]]` for `0 <= topk_ids[t,j] < E`; otherwise output `-1`. `R` and `E` are the routing-table row count and logical expert count.
-    - Recording: let `C = expert_tokens.numel()` and `s = local_expert_start`. For `group_list_type=1`, `count[i] = expert_tokens[i]`. For type 0, `count[0] = expert_tokens[0]` and `count[i] = expert_tokens[i] - expert_tokens[i-1]`. When `record_enabled != 0`, `expert_load_view[s+i] += count[i]`; otherwise load is unchanged. Integer-width semantics are described below.
-- **Algorithm flow**:
-    1. Each program maps one contiguous tile of flattened token and top-k assignments. For up to 2048 assignments the tile size is 64, for up to 8192 it is 128, and for larger inputs it is 1024.
-    2. Each lane derives the routing row from its token index, masks invalid logical expert IDs, and writes one physical ID. The last tile masks assignments beyond the end of the input.
-    3. Existing MoE dispatch and computation produce `expert_tokens`. Recording uses blocks of `B = min(256, next_power_of_2(C))` experts and `ceil(C / B)` programs. Each program reads the device-side flag, decodes counts and updates its disjoint load range. Type 0 reads the previous global element across block boundaries. Neither kernel uses global atomics.
-- **Supported modes**: Eager execution and ACL graph capture/replay on Ascend NPU. The optimized kernels were validated on Atlas A3 and Ascend 950DT.
-
-## Parameters
-
-All public entry-point parameters below are required. `T` is the token count, `K` is the routing slot count, `P` is the physical expert-load size, and `C` is the local expert count.
-
-### map_to_physical_triton
-
-| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| `topk_ids` | Input | Logical expert IDs `[T, K]` | int32 / int64 | Contiguous ND |
-| `expert_replica_routing_table` | Input | Runtime logical-to-physical table `[R, E]` | int32 | Contiguous ND |
-| Return value | Output | Physical IDs `[T, K]`; invalid logical IDs produce `-1` | Same as `topk_ids` | Contiguous ND |
-
-### record_expert_tokens_triton
-
-| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| `expert_tokens` | Input | MoE-provided counts or cumulative counts `[C]` | int32 / int64 | Contiguous 1-D |
-| `expert_load_view` | Input / Output | Cumulative physical-domain load `[P]`; only `[s, s+C)` is updated | int32 / int64 | Contiguous 1-D |
-| `record_enabled` | Input | Device scalar; false disables load updates | bool | Scalar |
-| `group_list_type` | Attribute | `1` for counts; `0` for cumulative counts | Python int | Scalar |
-| `local_expert_start` | Attribute | Start `s` of the local physical-expert range | Python int | Scalar |
-| Return value | Output | N/A; updates the load in place | None | N/A |
-
-## Constraints
-
-- Tensors must use contiguous storage on the same NPU. Arbitrary strides and overlapping source/destination buffers are not supported.
-- Mapping requires 2-D IDs and a 2-D table. For nonempty IDs, `R > 0` and `E > 0`; physical IDs in the table must be representable by the output dtype. The kernel masks invalid logical IDs but does not validate table contents. Empty IDs return without a kernel launch.
-- Recording requires 1-D counts/load, `group_list_type` in `{0, 1}`, and `0 <= s <= s+C <= P`. The flag is a device scalar, not a host boolean. Empty counts return without a kernel launch.
-- If counts are wider than the load dtype, operands are narrowed before arithmetic; add/subtract is equivalent modulo the destination width. Otherwise cumulative-count subtraction retains the input width before adding to the destination, preserving existing overflow semantics. Floating-point tolerance is N/A.
-- Mapping specializes `TOPK` and `BLOCK_SIZE` to simplify token indexing and set the vector width. `numel` is a runtime bound with value specialization disabled. Triton still distinguishes pointer dtype and alignment, integer types and the default scalar classes of `num_logical_experts` and `routing_table_rows`.
-- The MoE factory registers the map wrapper for EPLB-enabled V2 routers inside the model runner's JIT registry window. The worker compiles six keys per logical expert count and top-k, covering three tiles and int32/int64 IDs for the standard aligned, contiguous int32 routing table with 1024 rows. The same wrapper and launch specification serve runtime calls. Other pointer alignment classes or routing-table scalar classes can compile on first use.
-- `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` controls startup compilation and defaults to `True`. See [Triton JIT warmup on Ascend](../../../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/triton_jit_warmup.md) for registration and validation details. Recording uses lazy compilation with `group_list_type` and its block size as compile-time parameters.
-- Graph replay retains captured shapes, addresses, launch dimensions and host scalar arguments. Routing-table contents and the device-side record flag may change in the same buffers before replay; both are read on device without `.item()`.
-- Recording accumulates the counts supplied by EPLB. Padding exclusion, where applicable, takes place before the operator receives those counts.
-
-## Origin and Differences
-
-- **Origin**: Optimizes the existing Ascend EPLB kernels in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/eplb.py`, called through the shared EPLB custom operators in `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/eplb.py`.
-- **Differences**:
-    - The flat map distributes contiguous assignments across programs and keeps the input ID width. Assignment counts of the same scalar type share a variant within a tile bucket when the other specialization inputs match.
-    - Recording splits experts into blocks of at most 256, preserves the cumulative-count dependency across blocks, and avoids wider-than-needed arithmetic when the load dtype is narrower.
-    - The public ABI, runtime table lookup, cumulative load updates, record-off behavior and post-MoE recording boundary are unchanged. No model-specific integration is added.
-
-## Test Cases
-
-The nightly NPU suite checks exact integer equality (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`) against independent PyTorch indexing and count-decoding references.
-
-- Mapping covers Qwen3-30B-A3B decode and prefill, additional `(E, K) = (896, 16)` geometry, both ID dtypes, invalid IDs, table wrapping, and tile tails and transitions.
-- Recording covers `C = 64/255/256/257/896`, both group-list types, all int32/int64 count/load combinations, integer wraparound, nonzero initial loads and local starts, and record-off behavior.
-- Graph replay reads updated routing-table contents and the record flag from the same device buffers.
-- CPU warmup tests cover enabled-router registration, registry-window scope, deduplication, metadata-only compilation and runtime dispatch at the tile boundaries.
-
-The Qwen3-30B-A3B W8A8 workload used TP2/EP2. Observed mapping inputs were int32 `[33, 8]` and `[32, 8]` in prefill and `[1, 8]` in decode. Recording used int64 `[64]` counts and int32 `[128]` load with local starts 0 and 64. The PR description records the measurement revisions and conditions.
-

-pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_eplb.py
-pytest -q tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_eplb_map_warmup.py
-```

[Performance] Integrate union GBSA prefill for Qwen4Exp (#21627)

Fuse sparse-index preparation for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GBSA Prefill and
call the official GBSA metadata and attention operators.

## Performance results

### 128K input / 1-token output

#### A3

Both versions used the same Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8 weights, 8 A3 NPUs
(TP2×PP4), and the same PP4 fixes. TTFT was averaged over the same five
requests per version after warm-up at concurrency 1. The measured prefix
cache hit rate was **88.87%** for both versions.

| Metric | Unit | Before (main) | After (GBSA Union) | Change | Change
rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | ms | 1935.8 | 1699.0 | −236.7 | **−12.23%** |

#### A5

Both versions used the same Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8-MXFP weights, 4 A5
NPUs (TP2×DP2, PP1), and the same operator runtime dependencies, with EP
enabled and MTP disabled. TTFT was averaged over the same five requests
per version after warm-up at concurrency 1. The measured prefix cache
hit rate was **88.87%** for both versions. All requests completed
successfully.

| Metric | Unit | Before (main) | After (GBSA Union) | Change | Change
rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | ms | 2278.4 | 1938.5 | −339.9 | **−14.92%** |

The A5 comparison used main commit `03f69b977` and PR commit
`c02252e80`. A3 and A5 results are platform-specific comparisons; their
different parallel configurations do not support a direct comparison of
absolute latency across platforms.

### Full QSA module performance

Q=4096, KV=128K, TP2×PP1, including projections, LI V2, attention, and
TP communication.

| Platform | main | PR #21627 | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 | 22.858 ms | 16.875 ms | **26.17%** |
| A5 | 22.799 ms | 12.629 ms | **44.61%** |

Module tests use production weights and synthetic hidden states; these
are not end-to-end TTFT results.

### GPQA Diamond accuracy

The GBSA Union version was evaluated on all 198 questions with Thinking
enabled and the official recommended sampling parameters.

#### A3

Evaluated using 8 A3 NPUs (TP2×PP4).

| method | Correct | Incorrect | Accuracy | Truncated responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA | 179/198 | 19 | **90.40%** | 2 |

One truncated response was scored as correct because the answer
extractor matched the expected choice in the unfinished Thinking text.

#### A5

Evaluated using 4 A5 NPUs (TP2×DP2, PP1).

| method | Correct | Incorrect | Accuracy | Truncated responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA | 183/198 | 15 | **92.42%** | 1 |

The truncated response was scored as incorrect.

The A5 GPQA run used the image’s standard GBSA runtime, while the A5
TTFT runs used isolated GBSA/metadata runtime dependencies. The GPQA
result therefore does not validate the exact operator runtime
configuration used for the A5 TTFT comparison.

TP2×PP4 end-to-end testing requires the PP4 fixes from #20443.

+    compact[0, :3] = torch.tensor([base, base, base + 3])
+    compact[1, :2] = torch.tensor([base + 1, base])
+    visible = torch.tensor([4 * base + 9, 4 * base + 8, 4 * base + 11], dtype=torch.int32)
+    row_map = torch.tensor([[0, 1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1], [2, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1]], dtype=torch.int32)
+    width = 8 * (input_groups + 1)
+    indices = torch.full((1, 2, width), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices[0, 0, :3] = torch.tensor([base, base + 1, base + 2])
+    indices[0, 1, 0] = base + 2
+    mask = torch.zeros((1, 2, width * 4), dtype=torch.int32)
+    mask[0, 0, :9] = torch.tensor([3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1])

+    rows = 4096

+    private = 512 + torch.arange(8)[:, None] * 128 + torch.arange(128)
+    compact[:, 384:512] = private.repeat(rows // 8, 1)
+    # Each lane replaces its last private block with the same one-token tail.

+    row_map = torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1, 8)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Experimental prefill-only union GBSA integration for Qwen4Exp.
+
+The official transformer operator package is required; decode keeps the stock GBSA path.
+Union construction stays on the device, including the exact per-query mask.
+"""
+
+from types import ModuleType
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+UNION_SIZE = 8
+BLOCK_Y = 4
+INVALID_KEY = 1 << 30
+GBSA_PAGE_SIZE = 128
+
+
+def build_qsa_union_inputs_from_compact(
+    compact_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    visible: torch.Tensor,
+    group_row_map: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Build Union inputs with the native AscendC operator."""
+    return torch.ops._C_ascend.qsa_union_inputs(
+        compact_indices.contiguous(), visible.contiguous(), group_row_map.contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+def _build_qsa_union_inputs_torch(
+    sparse_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    sparse_count: torch.Tensor,
+    visible: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Group one request without altering its selected blocks or tail policy."""
+    if sparse_idx.ndim != 3 or sparse_idx.shape[0] != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Union preparation requires one KV head")
+    rows, topk = sparse_idx.shape[1:]
+    groups = (rows + UNION_SIZE - 1) // UNION_SIZE
+    width = UNION_SIZE * topk
+    padded = torch.full((groups * UNION_SIZE, topk), INVALID_KEY, dtype=torch.int32, device=sparse_idx.device)
+    columns = torch.arange(topk, device=sparse_idx.device)
+    lanes = torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=sparse_idx.device).remainder(UNION_SIZE)
+    valid = (columns.unsqueeze(0) < sparse_count[0].unsqueeze(1)) & (sparse_idx[0] >= 0)
+    padded[:rows] = torch.where(valid, sparse_idx[0] * UNION_SIZE + lanes.unsqueeze(1), INVALID_KEY)
+    sorted_keys = padded.reshape(groups, width).float().sort(dim=-1).values
+    keys = sorted_keys.to(torch.int32)
+    # Scaling the already-FP32 sort keys by a power of two is exact. All keys
+    # are nonnegative; conversion to int32 therefore gives floor(key / 8).
+    block_id = (sorted_keys * (1.0 / UNION_SIZE)).to(torch.int32)
+    valid = keys < INVALID_KEY
+    previous = torch.nn.functional.pad(keys[:, :-1], (1, 0), value=-1)
+    previous_block = torch.nn.functional.pad(block_id[:, :-1], (1, 0), value=-1)
+    first = valid & (block_id != previous_block)
+    rank = first.cumsum(-1, dtype=torch.int32) - 1
+    union_count = (rank[:, -1] + 1).unsqueeze(0)
+    destinations = torch.where(valid, rank, width).long()
+    table = torch.full((groups, width + 1), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=sparse_idx.device)
+    # All duplicate destinations have the same block ID. Invalid entries write
+    # only to a discarded sentinel column, never to the last valid union block.
+    table.scatter_(1, destinations, torch.where(valid, block_id, -1))
+    union_idx = table[:, :width].contiguous().unsqueeze(0)
+    if rows % UNION_SIZE == 0:
+        padded_visible = visible
+    else:
+        padded_visible = torch.zeros(groups * UNION_SIZE, dtype=visible.dtype, device=visible.device)
+        padded_visible[:rows] = visible
+    query_lane = keys.remainder(UNION_SIZE)
+    visible_rows = padded_visible.reshape(groups, UNION_SIZE)
+    query_lane_long = query_lane.long()
+    row_visible = visible_rows.gather(1, query_lane_long)
+    unique = valid & (keys != previous)
+    bit_table = torch.tensor([1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128], dtype=torch.int32, device=sparse_idx.device)
+    bit_rows = bit_table.unsqueeze(0).expand(groups, -1).contiguous()
+    bits = bit_rows.gather(1, query_lane_long)
+    # Full 4-token blocks share one bitset. Only the at-most-one partial
+    # block per query requires per-token handling.
+    full = unique & ((block_id + 1) * BLOCK_Y <= row_visible)
+    full_mask = torch.zeros_like(table)
+    full_mask.scatter_add_(1, destinations, torch.where(full, bits, 0))
+    mask = full_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, -1, BLOCK_Y).contiguous()
+    mask = mask.reshape(groups, (width + 1) * BLOCK_Y)
+
+    tail_block = visible_rows.div(BLOCK_Y, rounding_mode="floor")
+    tail_key = tail_block * UNION_SIZE + torch.arange(UNION_SIZE, dtype=torch.int32, device=sparse_idx.device)
+    location = torch.searchsorted(keys, tail_key).clamp_max(width - 1)
+    found = keys.gather(1, location) == tail_key
+    tail_rank = rank.gather(1, location)
+    tail_length = visible_rows.remainder(BLOCK_Y)
+    partial = found & (tail_length > 0)
+    token = torch.arange(BLOCK_Y, dtype=torch.int32, device=sparse_idx.device)
+    allowed_tail = partial.unsqueeze(-1) & (token < tail_length.unsqueeze(-1))
+    tail_dest = torch.where(partial, tail_rank, width).long().unsqueeze(-1) * BLOCK_Y + token
+    tail_bits = torch.where(allowed_tail, bit_table.reshape(1, UNION_SIZE, 1), 0)
+    mask.scatter_add_(
+        1, tail_dest.reshape(groups, UNION_SIZE * BLOCK_Y), tail_bits.reshape(groups, UNION_SIZE * BLOCK_Y)
+    )
+    exact = mask[:, : width * BLOCK_Y].contiguous().unsqueeze(0)
+
+    return union_idx, union_count, exact
+
+
+def _run_union_gbsa(
+    union_ops: ModuleType,
+    query: torch.Tensor,
+    key_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    value_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    union_inputs: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
+    cu_q: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    output: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    max_query_length: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Use the same native attention contract for single and packed requests."""
+    kv_heads = key_cache.shape[2]
+    q_heads = query.shape[1]
+    if kv_heads < 1 or q_heads < 1 or q_heads % kv_heads or q_heads // kv_heads > 16:
+        raise ValueError("Union GBSA requires 1 to 16 Q heads per KV head and evenly sized head groups")
+    if kv_heads > 1:
+        # The QSA indexer selects the same blocks for all KV heads.
+        union_inputs = tuple(t.expand(kv_heads, *t.shape[1:]).contiguous() for t in union_inputs)
+    union_idx, union_count, exact = union_inputs
+    common = dict(
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_q,
+        seqused_kv=seq_lens,
+        layout_q="TND",
+        layout_kv="PA_BBND",
+        layout_sparse_pattern=4,
+        mask_mode=3,
+        quant_mode=0,
+        softmax_precision=0,
+        win_left=-1,
+        win_right=-1,
+        residual_block_mode=0,
+        is_consistent_topk=False,
+    )
+    shape = [UNION_SIZE, BLOCK_Y]
+    metadata = union_ops.generic_block_sparse_attention_metadata(
+        union_idx,
+        union_count,
+        q_heads,
+        kv_heads,
+        query.shape[-1],
+        shape,
+        max_seqlen_q=max_query_length,
+        max_seqlen_kv=block_table.shape[1] * GBSA_PAGE_SIZE,
+        **common,
+    )
+    result, _ = union_ops.generic_block_sparse_attention(
+        query.contiguous(),
+        key_cache,
+        value_cache,
+        union_idx,
+        union_count,
+        shape,
+        metadata=metadata,
+        block_table=block_table.contiguous(),
+        attn_mask=exact,
+        softmax_scale=query.shape[-1] ** -0.5,
+        return_softmax_lse=False,
+        **common,
+    )
+    output.copy_(result)
+    return output
+
+
+def qsa_union_gbsa_attention(
+    query: torch.Tensor,
+    key_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    value_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    compact_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    token_to_req: torch.Tensor,
+    logical_positions: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    output: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    request_index: int,
+    prepared: Any,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Lazy import isolates the optional vendor package from model discovery and
+    # from stock decode/graph capture. Missing support must fail visibly.
+    from vllm_ascend.ops import gbsa as union_ops
+
+    if block_table.shape[1] * GBSA_PAGE_SIZE > (1 << 23):
+        raise ValueError("Union index encoding exceeds exact FP32 sort range")
+    union_inputs = build_qsa_union_inputs_from_compact(
+        compact_indices, prepared.visible_lengths, prepared.group_row_map
+    )
+    cu_q = prepared.cu_q
+    selected_lengths = prepared.seq_lens
+    selected_table = prepared.block_table
+    max_query_length = prepared.max_query_length
+    return _run_union_gbsa(
+        union_ops,
+        query,
+        key_cache,
+        value_cache,
+        union_inputs,
+        cu_q,
+        selected_lengths,
+        selected_table,
+        output,
+        max_query_length=max_query_length,
+    )
+
+
+def qsa_union_gbsa_attention_batch(
+    query: torch.Tensor,
+    key_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    value_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    compact_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    token_to_req: torch.Tensor,
+    logical_positions: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    output: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    query_starts: tuple[int, ...],
+    request_indices: tuple[int, ...],
+    prepared: Any,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Run adjacent packed Prefill requests in one union GBSA launch."""
+    from vllm_ascend.ops import gbsa as union_ops
+
+    if not request_indices or len(request_indices) + 1 != len(query_starts):
+        raise ValueError("Each packed query segment must have one request")
+    if block_table.shape[1] * GBSA_PAGE_SIZE > (1 << 23):
+        raise ValueError("Union index encoding exceeds exact FP32 sort range")
+    union_inputs = build_qsa_union_inputs_from_compact(
+        compact_indices, prepared.visible_lengths, prepared.group_row_map
+    )
+    cu_q = prepared.cu_q
+    table = prepared.block_table
+    lengths = prepared.seq_lens
+    max_query_length = prepared.max_query_length
+    return _run_union_gbsa(
+        union_ops,
+        query,
+        key_cache,
+        value_cache,
+        union_inputs,
+        cu_q,
+        lengths,
+        table,
+        output,
+        max_query_length=max_query_length,
+    )

+# prepare_qsa_visible_lengths
+
+## Description
+
+- **Function**: Compute the causal KV length visible to each live query row. The Qwen4Exp worker prepares it once per step so Union Prefill layers can share it.
+- **Formula**: For row `i`, normalize a negative request index by adding the number of requests once. For a valid index `r`, write `min(max(position[i] + 1, 0), seq_lens[r])`. Otherwise write zero.
+- **Algorithm flow**: One Triton program loads one row's position and request, gathers the sequence length with a validity mask, then writes one int32 value.
+- **Supported modes**: Qwen4Exp GBSA Union metadata preparation on Ascend. The wrapper accepts an existing device buffer.
+
+## Parameters
+
+| Parameter | Direction | Description | Type | Format |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| logical_positions | Input | Zero-based logical position per row | int32 or int64 | 1D, strided |
+| seq_lens | Input | Nonnegative current KV length per request | int32 | 1D, strided |
+| token_to_req | Input | Row-to-request mapping | int32 or int64 | 1D, strided |
+| visible_lengths | Output | Caller-owned buffer | int32 | 1D, contiguous |
+| rows | Attribute | A Python integer specifying how many query rows to process. | Host-side Python `int` | Scalar |
+
+## Constraints
+
+All tensors reside on the same NPU. Positions and their increments must fit in int32.
+`rows` must be nonnegative and fit in both row inputs and the output. Only the first
+`rows` output elements are written. Zero rows skip the launch. The worker reuses a
+device buffer across layers. The wrapper reads shapes and strides on the host and
+does not copy tensor values back to the host.
+
+## Origin and Differences
+
+Developed for the vLLM-Ascend Qwen4Exp Union Prefill path. It combines indexed
+length lookup and causal clipping in a single kernel and writes into preallocated
+storage. Upstream vLLM operator equivalent: N/A.
+
+## Test Cases
+
+Run `pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_prepare_qsa_visible_lengths.py`.
+The tests require exact integer equality for a 4096-row chunk at 128K KV, a partial
+chunk, multiple requests, strided inputs, invalid request IDs and empty input.
+
+## Example
+
+For positions `[2, 9, 6]`, request IDs `[0, 1, -1]` and sequence lengths
+`[4, 7]`, the three visible lengths are `[3, 7, 7]`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Prepare per-query visible KV lengths for Qwen4Exp Union Prefill."""
+
+import torch
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _prepare_qsa_visible_lengths_kernel(
+    positions,
+    lengths,
+    requests,
+    visible_lengths,
+    position_stride,
+    length_stride,
+    request_stride,
+    requests_count,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    request = tl.load(requests + row * request_stride).to(tl.int64)
+    request = tl.where(request < 0, request + requests_count, request)
+    valid_request = (request >= 0) & (request < requests_count)
+    safe_request = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(request, 0), requests_count - 1)
+    position = tl.load(positions + row * position_stride).to(tl.int32)
+    length = tl.load(lengths + safe_request * length_stride, mask=valid_request, other=0).to(tl.int32)
+    tl.store(visible_lengths + row, tl.minimum(tl.maximum(position + 1, 0), length))
+
+
+def prepare_qsa_visible_lengths(
+    logical_positions: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    token_to_req: torch.Tensor,
+    visible_lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    rows: int,
+) -> None:
+    """Prepare only visibility for Prefill Union-GBSA once per model step."""
+    if rows < 0 or rows > logical_positions.shape[0] or rows > token_to_req.shape[0]:
+        raise ValueError("QSA prepared row count exceeds input capacity")
+    if visible_lengths.shape[0] < rows:
+        raise ValueError("QSA visible-length buffer is too small")
+    if rows == 0:
+        return
+    _prepare_qsa_visible_lengths_kernel[(rows,)](
+        logical_positions,
+        seq_lens,
+        token_to_req,
+        visible_lengths,
+        logical_positions.stride(0),
+        seq_lens.stride(0),
+        token_to_req.stride(0),
+        seq_lens.shape[0],
+        num_warps=1,
+    )

[Feature][Model] Enable Qwen3.8 Flash Next PP and SP (#20311)

## Summary

Enable Qwen3.8 Flash Next (Qwen4-Exp) pipeline parallelism (PP),
sequence parallelism (SP/FlashComm1), MTP speculative decoding, and
pipeline-disaggregated three-tier KV-cache pooling on Model Runner V2.

This is a thin current-`main` adaptation. The PR is validated with vLLM
main commit
[`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15).

## Design and changes

### Qwen3.8 Next PP, SP, and MTP

- Enable FlashComm1/SP for Qwen3.8 Flash Next.
- Preserve PP-stage ownership across model state and intermediate-tensor
transport.
- Keep the optimized target-model QSA fused RMSNorm + MRoPE projection
while selecting the graph-safe decomposition for `mtp.` draft layers.
This avoids sending the MTP drafter through the target-only projection
path and prevents Q/K NaNs and draft-acceptance regressions.
- Size packed QSA/GDN/PLE cache slots for the largest physical state
group and allow a global cache group to have no local layers on a PP
stage.
- Use persistent request-slot indexing for Mamba state copies so
reordered or sparse batches cannot read or write another request's
SSM/conv state.

### Minimal MRV2 token alignment

`pad_num_tokens()` is the single policy entry that computes the physical
token-row count required by TP-shared execution.

- Graph initialization aligns each capture size before constructing
graph grids.
- Eager execution aligns `num_scheduled_tokens` before DP
synchronization and batch-descriptor construction.
- The scheduler retains the logical token limit while runner buffers and
graph capacity use the aligned physical limit. With TP4 and a logical
limit of 4097, the scheduler admits at most 4097 real tokens and the
physical capacity is 4100 rows.
- `batch_req_state.num_tokens` remains the logical count and
`batch_desc.num_tokens` remains the selected physical execution width.
- Padding rows in `input_ids` and `positions` are zeroed before full
physical buffers are consumed.

Padding is not moved into model-specific SP/PCP code, and
scheduler-visible request capacity is unchanged.

### Generic PP-local cache-group projection for AscendStore

vLLM preserves global KV-cache group IDs across workers while a
worker-local projection may legitimately contain `layer_names=[]`.
AscendStore now follows that contract without identifying PLE or a
particular model:

- `project_group_ids()` maps request-global group IDs to groups with
real local regions before synchronous GET, asynchronous PUT, and
asynchronous GET build transfer descriptors. Empty local groups never
produce `layerNum=0` descriptors.
- `_collect_group_pp_ranks()` gathers which PP ranks own each global
group. Lookup keys are generated only for real owners, preventing false
misses on keys that a non-owner PP rank never wrote.
- Global group order and IDs remain unchanged; only each worker's
physical I/O view is projected.

This is generic for any model whose global cache group is empty on some
PP stages, including singleton PLE and future layouts.

### Torch utility adaptation

The common `get_npu_view_from_cpu_tensor` behavior is provided through
the Ascend patch layer, with behavioral tests for the bound Core
function, operator call, and pinned-memory validation.

## Relationship to cache-group interleaving (#22327)

[#22327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22327) is
already in the current base. It changes compatible Qwen3.8 Next GDN
owners from contiguous chunks to `members[i::num_groups]`. Under
standard continuous PP partitioning, ordinary GDN groups are distributed
across every stage (`6/6` for PP2 and `3/3/3/3` for PP4), instead of
producing layouts such as `13/0` or `0/10`.

#22327 improves ordinary-group distribution. This PR independently makes
the AscendStore connector honor the general vLLM contract that a global
group may still be empty on a worker.

## Validation

### Unit and static checks

- Related CPU unit-test set before the final rebase: **497 passed, 2
skipped**.
- Current rebased head: pre-commit, Ruff/formatting, three-version mypy,
DCO, conflict checks, test selection, documentation builds, and both CPU
UT matrices pass.
- The selected NPU CI matrix is still running.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- The PR remains one signed-off commit on top of current `main`.

### Earlier three-run 16-NPU benchmark data

These measurements are retained from the previous PR description. Each
workload ran three times with 2 prompts, concurrency 2, unlimited
request rate, temperature 0, and seed 7. Every strategy/workload
combination completed all 6 requests with 0 failures. A result cell is
`mean TTFT (ms) / mean TPOT (ms) / output throughput (token/s)`.

### Earlier Decode-PP-off three-run follow-up

This retained follow-up removed PP from Decode for the PP

[BugFix][PCP] Compact decoder replay across PCP ranks on prefix hits (#22453)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #22416.

With prefill context parallelism (`PCP > 1`), prefix caching and
`--swa-bounded-replay`, a cache hit can return an immediate EOS
(`token_ids=[1]`)
instead of the expected continuation. Cold prefills and PCP=1 hits are
fine.

Root cause: `DecoderReplayState._pcp_kept_lengths` decides whether the
compact
decoder replay saves rows by comparing the **global** kept row count
with the
**PCP rank-local** padded token extent:

```python
num_padded = int(global_kept.sum())                 # 128
if num_padded >= batch.num_tokens_after_padding:    # 30 on PCP8
    return None
```

A prefix hit schedules the hit's last replay window plus the uncached
tail, and
PCP spreads that query across ranks (e.g. 234 tokens -> 24-30 rows per
rank on
PCP8). The global window (128) is therefore larger than the local padded
width
(30), so the function returns `None`, the compact replay is skipped, and
layers
21-39 run in the ordinary PCP main pass with the scheduler's replay
floor
instead of the compact replay floor. Cold prefills (local width ~1246)
and
PCP=1 hits (local width 234) take the compact replay, which is why only
PCP>1
hits break.

This PR removes the rank-local comparison. Compaction is a global
decision:
if any request is trimmed, the PCP branch compacts, the same rule the
non-PCP
path uses (`requires_compaction`). The rank-local padded width is not a
valid
proxy for it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a correctness fix for an existing opt-in feature
(`swa_bounded_replay` with `PCP > 1`). Prefix caching off and PCP=1 are
inert:
`DecoderReplayState` is only constructed when bounded replay is enabled,
and
`_pcp_kept_lengths` returns early when there is no PCP context. No
release note
fragment is needed.

### How was this patch tested?

Tests in `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_state.py`:

- `_pcp_kept_lengths` on a prefix hit split across PCP ranks (PCP2 and
PCP4,
with `local_token_indices`), where each rank's padded width is no larger
than
the global replay window. It checks the kept rows per rank, including
the
  owner of the tail, the rank before it, and a rank that owns none.
- A `prepare()`-level test (without stubbing `_pcp_kept_lengths`)
asserting that
the same prefix hit reaches the compact PCP replay (`layers.rows` is
set).

Both fail with the old rank-local comparison.

End-to-end validation on 16x 910B2C (A2), TP1 / DP2 / PCP8 / EP16, 1M
context,
MBT 16384, utilization 0.93, `--enable-prefix-caching
--swa-bounded-replay`:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 8K passphrase cold | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` |
| 8K passphrase hit | EOS, `token_ids=[1]` | `Q7X-4921-KLM` |
| 32K passphrase cold | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` | `Q7X-4921-KLM.` |
| 32K passphrase hit | EOS | identical to cold, ids
`[51,25,58,15,25880,19,12496,39851,16,1]` |

After the fix, the hit trace takes the compact replay
(`uses_pcp_replay=True`, `replay_start=[9834]`).

The unit tests in this file pass on CPU. `ruff check`, `ruff format`,
and the
repository pre-commit hooks pass on the two changed files.

### Checklist

- [x] **Regression test**: added tests that fail with the old rank-local
  comparison and pass with the fix.
- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the tests cover PCP ownership
of the
  replay window (owner of the tail, owner before it, no owner) and the
`prepare()` wiring; the existing tests cover owner-before-tail,
owner-of-tail,
  and prompt-logprob rows (no compaction).
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: not applicable to this pure
planning
  calculation.
- [x] **Performance impact**: cold prefills keep the ordinary replay
unless
compacting actually reduces rows on each rank. The decision now compacts
when
a trimmed request has cached context (a prefix hit spreads the replay
window
across PCP ranks and must be re-indexed) or when the global kept width
is
smaller than one PCP rank's shard width (`ceil(global_extent /
pcp_size)`),
a global value so every rank in the group makes the same decision. A
short

[Performance][Qwen4Exp] Write GBSA results directly to caller output (#22375)

## What this PR optimizes

Generic Block Sparse Attention previously allocated its own output
tensor and the QSA caller copied that same-shape result into the
graph-owned attention buffer, producing an extra TensorMove after GBSA.

This PR adds a caller-owned output path so GBSA writes directly into the
final attention buffer.

The branch is based directly on `upstream/main` at
`c12397a088f7e63ed9defae66ac98faffee88b81` and has no dependency on
#22373 or any GDN PR.

## Optimization points

- Add `npu_generic_block_sparse_attention_out` to the C++ ACLNN adapter.
- Validate caller output shape, dtype, device, and contiguity before
dispatch.
- Register PrivateUse1 and Meta implementations for the out variant.
- Add a Python `generic_block_sparse_attention_out` wrapper while
preserving the existing allocating API.
- Update the Qwen4Exp GBSA caller to pass its graph-owned output buffer
directly.
- Remove the post-GBSA `output.copy_(result)` path that generated the
same-shape TensorMove.
- Keep softmax-LSE behavior and the existing API available for other
callers.

## Scope boundaries

- No QSA metadata preparation or Indexer multi-stream changes.
- No GDN changes.
- Includes the required user-facing performance release note in
`release_notes/fragments/22375.yaml`.

## Validation

- Python bytecode compilation for all three changed Python files:
passed.
- `ruff format --check`: passed.
- `ruff check`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Pairwise `git merge-tree --write-tree` checks against every other
functional branch completed without conflicts; no stacked PR is
required.

C++ build, A5 numerical comparison, ACL Graph replay, and profiler
confirmation that the GBSA-output TensorMove is absent remain required
before merge.

[BugFix][KVTransfer] Fix Mooncake group selection and PP reformat (#18476)

### What this PR does / why we need it

When P and D use different KV-head partitions, Mooncake must reformat
the received KV blocks before decode can use them. Two receiver bugs can
break this conversion:

- Cache selection parsed model layer numbers across all caches, allowing
a single-tensor index cache to enter a two-tensor K/V reformat group, or
omitting draft caches with reassigned transfer indices. Select the exact
registered transfer group's names and indices, intersected with the
current layer subset.
- Pending reformat descriptors were assigned by request ID and CP shard.
Multiple P PP stages contributing different layers to the same shard
overwrote each other's descriptors, leaving only the last stored segment
to be reformatted. Accumulate every PP segment under the existing lock
and retain the existing all-pulls-complete barrier, consume-once
behavior, and failure cleanup.

The second bug can return HTTP 200 with incorrect output because the KV
bytes arrive but some layers retain the transfer layout. PP4-to-PP1
alone does not require head-layout conversion; the reproduced case is P
TP4/PP4 to D TP2/PP1.

### Validation

- 34 targeted CPU regressions passed with the actual PR connector
imported in an existing Ascend runtime: 25 PP regressions plus the
original 9 cache-group selection cases.
- Negative control: the same 25 PP cases all fail on the unmodified PR
head.
- PP cases cover all 24 PP4 registration orders, two CP shards,
consume/clear exactly once, concurrent writers, and request isolation.
- Ruff lint and format checks passed for the changed connector and new
test.
- The same accumulation fix was previously validated on 2026-11-18 on
Ascend A3, with P TP4/PP4 and D TP2/DP16 across two decode hosts,
retaining MRV2, EAGLE3 and D FULL_DECODE_ONLY: 20/20 functional PD
requests correct (12/20 with only the group-selection fix), including
two long-input string retrieval cases; paired cold-cache
PD/local-prefill checks 4/4 correct. This was functional validation, not
a performance or GPQA result.
- Rebased the three existing fix/test commits unchanged onto main
`e445f28a29597aefe85b14abb72eea8a326b3082` on 2026-11-25 (`git
range-diff` confirms patch equivalence).
- Full CPU CI on rebased head `cdcf93b7a34b185883aa8b0fa376520bad29d097`
passed: [vLLM main
`c410543d`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45563750944/job/139034939276):
**22,889 passed, 131 skipped**; [vLLM
v0.34.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45563750944/job/139034939205):
**22,884 passed, 136 skipped**. Each lane passed all 34 PR-specific
regressions.
-
[Pre-commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45563750944/job/139033414828),
including format/lint and Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 type checks, and DCO
passed on this head. The hardware figures above remain the earlier
validation; no new NPU run is claimed for this rebase.

### User-facing change

Keep heterogeneous cache groups separate and reformat all transferred PP
layer segments before reporting receive completion. No new flags or
wire-format changes.

[Feature][Model] Add Kimi fine-grained projection and shared-expert TP (#21624) ### What this PR does / why we need it? Reduce per-device Kimi-K3.1 projection and shared-expert weight storage by sharding selected weights over independent DP-axis groups. Attention, convolution and recurrent state remain on the original request owner. - **Reuse GLM projection infrastructure:** GLM and Kimi share input-capacity preparation and QKV/beta owner restoration through `KDAInputProjectionTPLayout`. GLM retains its fused projection, owner-local F/G work and eager execution. GLM checks KDA head divisibility during startup configuration validation. The same configuration block accepts Kimi-K3.1 by its outer model type, and Kimi checks its head layout in the KDA layer. - **Keep Kimi-specific computation local:** mixed MXFP8 QKV and BF16 beta/F/G loading and multistream scheduling stay in the existing Kimi implementation. Kimi KDA localTP runs directly in the layer for full-graph decode. The main stream runs QKV input quantization, QKV quantized matmul and BF16 beta projection consecutively in that order. At the first recurrent KDA or RecoverSSM kernel, the auxiliary stream computes G and exchanges its head shards. The main stream joins before gated normalization. An idle owner still participates in the gate collective. DSA joins its gate after attention. Both paths use the common head layout. Existing KDA Column/Merged linears accept an explicit group and retain their loaders; no duplicate projection Linear classes or new `ops/finegrained_tp.py` file remain. - **Reuse output/public paths:** Public SFA detects the selected `OProjRowParallelOp` and uses the pre-trim token capacity for its existing exchange and reduction. GLM and Kimi SFA ranks with uneven batches or no local queries join the same O collectives. LM head, embedding and dense MLP retain their existing common execution paths, without chunk executors or Kimi-specific MLP/embedding graph operators. - **Shared experts:** partition gate/up outputs and matching down inputs, gather owner inputs, reuse scheme-owned quantization/local MLP, then perform one RS(sum) back to each owner. Linears do not repeat activation collectives. Models without latent transforms use the common runner; Kimi retains its latent-projection scheduling windows. Routed EP remains independent. Equal-size DP-axis groups reuse one coordinator; teardown destroys aliases once. The old active graph check stays in input preparation. A small inherited idle check covers both default and Mamba model-state entries before collectives; no dynamic `cudagraph_manager` attribute, dispatch callback or warmup context is added. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Seven independent sizes under `additional_config.finegrained_tp_config`, defaulting to 1; 0/1 disable a split: ```json { "finegrained_tp_config": { "qkv_iproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "gproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "oproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "mlp_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "embedding_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "lmhead_tensor_parallel_size": 8, "shared_expert_tensor_parallel_size": 8 }, "enable_shared_expert_dp": false, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "scheduler_config": {"recompute_scheduler_enable": true} } ``` This is additional configuration, not a complete launch command. Configure the KV connector chain separately. - Sizes must divide DP size. The existing MoE-only restriction remains because dense workers do not preserve the required DP group. Projection knobs require model-side wiring. - GLM QKV-only retains TP=PCP=PP=1 and PD decode with explicit DP capacity padding. Kimi-specific graph and offload requirements do not apply to it. - Kimi QKV/G and shared TP require TP=PCP=DCP=PP=1, graph-dispatched PD decode, capture coverage including speculative slots, recompute scheduling and `PreemptOffloadConnector`. - Shared TP requires recognized partitioned gate/up/down linears and rejects shared-DP replication and LoRA. Fused shared MegaMoe stays disabled because its interface does not own the DP-axis AG/RS; routed MegaMoe remains independent. - Existing O/dense-MLP warning-and-disable behavior for insufficient capture coverage remains. Vocabulary topology/layout restrictions remain. Runtime idle MM ranks still join embedding collectives, preserving the captured buffer address. DSpark uses the DP-agreed query-pass decision when vocabulary TP is enabled; target projection synchronization does not pull dense drafters into unrelated collectives. +
+## Shared-expert fine-grained TP
+
+`shared_expert_tensor_parallel_size` independently shards the shared expert's
+gate/up output channels and matching down input channels along the DP axis.
+It does not enable dense MLP TP, change global TP, or change routed-expert EP
+placement. The default is `1`; `0` is also treated as disabled. Equal component
+sizes reuse a communicator, including when dense MLP TP is enabled separately.
+
+For example, on a DP32TP1 decode node, set:
+
+```json
+{
+  "finegrained_tp_config": {
+    "shared_expert_tensor_parallel_size": 8
+  },
+  "enable_shared_expert_dp": false,
+  "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true,
+  "scheduler_config": {
+    "recompute_scheduler_enable": true
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The activation flow for each group of eight DP owners is:
+
+```text
+local [T,H] -> AllGather [8T,H]
+  -> local gate/up weight shards -> activation -> local down weight shard
+  -> ReduceScatter(sum) -> original owner's complete [T,H] output
+```

+This also covers the A3 INT8-activation fused path, which directly invokes
+quantized matmuls, and 950DT Products MXFP paths, which retain their scheme-specific
+activation quantization and processed weight layouts. The shared-expert
+contribution stays on the separate branch when routed MegaMoe is used; its
+fused shared ABI does not implement these DP-axis collectives.
+
+With `multistream_overlap_shared_expert=true`, models providing routed input
+and output transforms, such as Kimi-K3's latent Down/Up projections, reuse the
+existing overlap windows: shared-input AllGather runs alongside latent Down,
+and shared-output ReduceScatter runs alongside latent Up. Input readiness is
+joined before routed EP collectives, and shared ReduceScatter waits for routed
+finalization before starting. Models without either transform use the regular
+input preparation/output join for the missing side; latent transforms are not
+a prerequisite. Profiling is needed to measure actual overlap and benefit.
+
+Requirements:
+
+- A MoE model using Ascend's shared runner and standard `gate_up_proj` /
+  `down_proj` linears, with the shared-expert prefix recognized by the linear
+  dispatcher. Incompatible shared modules fail explicitly during construction.
+- A3 or 950DT Products, global `TP=PCP=DCP=PP=1`, and a size evenly dividing DP.
+  The shared intermediate dimension must also divide evenly by the size.
+- P/D decode deployment with graph mode and capture capacity covering every
+  decode step, including speculative-token slots. Idle ranks still participate
+  with the graph's padded token capacity. Eager runtime dispatch is rejected.
+- Recompute scheduler and `PreemptOffloadConnector` in the connector chain,
+  configured as in the [preempt offload guide](preempt_offload_connector.md).
+- `enable_shared_expert_dp=false`; replicated shared weights and this sharding
+  mode are mutually exclusive. LoRA is not supported by this mode.
+
+Switching the new size back to `1` preserves the previous shared DP, global
+TP/SP and multistream paths. The existing dense-MLP size does not implicitly
+enable shared-expert sharding. No checkpoint conversion is required.

+from contextlib import contextmanager

+def test_dsa_gate_shares_stream_across_layers_and_waits_at_each_consumer(monkeypatch):
+    producer, project_stream, finish_stream, comm = (Mock() for _ in range(4))
+    create_stream = Mock(return_value=comm)
+    current = producer
+    trace = []
+    records = []
+    group = SimpleNamespace(world_size=2, device_group=object())
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def switch(stream):
+        nonlocal current
+        previous, current = current, stream
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            current = previous
+
+    def submit(name, received, send, process_group, async_op):
+        assert current is comm and process_group is group.device_group and async_op
+        trace.append(name)
+        # The work double must not keep a temporary send alive on behalf of the caller.
+        send_ref, received_ref = ref(send), ref(received)
+        assert (id(send), comm) in records
+
+        def wait():
+            trace.append((name, current))
+            assert send_ref() is not None
+            target = received_ref()
+            assert target is not None
+            target.fill_(1)
+
+        return SimpleNamespace(wait=wait)
+
+    def gather(received, send, group, async_op):
+        return submit("AG", received, send, group, async_op)
+
+    def exchange(received, send, group, async_op):
+        return submit("A2A", received, send, group, async_op)
+
+    def project(gathered):
+        assert current is project_stream and (id(gathered), current) in records
+        trace.append("project")
+        return (gathered + 1,)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.npu, "current_stream", lambda: current)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.npu, "Stream", create_stream)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kimi_k3, "_DSA_GATE_COMM_STREAMS", {})
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kimi_k3, "npu_stream_switch", switch)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, "record_stream", lambda tensor, stream: records.append((id(tensor), stream)))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.distributed, "all_gather_into_tensor", gather)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.distributed, "all_to_all_single", exchange)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kimi_k3.KDAInputProjectionTPLayout, "prepare_input", staticmethod(lambda x: (x, x.shape[0])))
+    first_layer = kimi_k3._make_dsa_gate_projection(project, group, 2, 2)
+    second_layer = kimi_k3._make_dsa_gate_projection(project, group, 2, 2)
+    hidden = torch.zeros(2, 4)[:, ::2]
+    create_stream.assert_not_called()
+    for begin_gate in (first_layer, second_layer, first_layer):
+        current = producer
+        project_gate = begin_gate(hidden)
+        assert trace == ["AG"]
+        current = project_stream
+        finish_gate = project_gate()
+        assert trace == ["AG", ("AG", project_stream), "project", "A2A"]
+        current = finish_stream
+        gate = finish_gate()
+        assert trace[-1] == ("A2A", finish_stream)
+        assert [stream for _, stream in records] == [
+            comm,
+            project_stream,
+            project_stream,
+            comm,
+            finish_stream,
+            finish_stream,
+        ]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(gate, torch.ones(2, 2, 2))
+        trace.clear()
+        records.clear()
+    create_stream.assert_called_once_with(device=hidden.device)
+    assert comm.wait_stream.call_args_list == [call(producer), call(project_stream)] * 3

[BugFix] Fix missing QLI V2 ACLNN arguments in A5 operator nightly (#23245)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix the QLI V2 LocalCandidates adapter used by the A5 single-card
operator nightly. The [failed nightly
job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/45572456963/job/139062735180)
crashes with exit code 139 in
`aclnnVllmAscendQuantLightningIndexerV2GetWorkspaceSize` while running
`test_quant_lightning_indexer_v2_dcp_matches_local_candidates_and_cpu_scores[0-7]`.

After #21394 extended the ACLNN signature, this adapter was missing the
optional `candidate_block_length` input and the
`candidate_block_length_out` output placeholder. Subsequent arguments
were therefore passed in the wrong positions.

Apply the same code change as #23240, preserving the original author
attribution:

- Pass `c10::nullopt` for the unused `candidate_block_length` input.
- Pass separate empty `int32` tensors for `candidate_topk_index_out` and
`candidate_block_length_out`.
- Keep both QLI V2 ACLNN call sites aligned with the 37-argument
signature.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes the LocalCandidates native call exercised by the A5 operator
nightly. The Python API, configuration, and returned `(indices, values)`
tuple stay the same. The omitted signature update was merged in #21394
on November 24 and is an unreleased main-branch regression, so no
separate release note fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff HEAD^ --check`: passed.
- Compared the modified header byte-for-byte with #23240: identical.
- Static call-site comparison: both ACLNN calls pass 37 arguments, with
the optional input and output slots aligned. The modified header uses LF
line endings.
- `bash format.sh ci`: attempted, then interrupted while pre-commit was
installing the actionlint environment; lint did not reach completion. CI
lint validation remains pending.
- MindIE's external `check_lf_eol.py --repo-root ...` check: failed on
the upstream repository's existing CRLF files and missing LF policy
configuration. The changed header itself is LF-only; unrelated upstream
files were left untouched.
- The existing nightly regression already exercises the failing
local-reference path, including an empty local shard and non-empty
lengths; no duplicate test was added.
- A5 runtime validation: **CI testing only, pending**. Re-run
`singlecard-ops-a5` against this PR and verify the existing
`test_quant_lightning_indexer_v2_dcp_matches_local_candidates_and_cpu_scores`
cases. No hardware or performance pass is claimed.

Pre-PR review: one adapter-only change; no new configuration, fallback,
timeout, synchronization, or workload-placement logic. The added output
tensor has zero elements, keeping device storage bounded.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage** — existing empty-shard and
non-empty nightly cases retained; A5 execution pending.
- [ ] **Regression test** — existing nightly test reproduces this
failure; no new test added.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage** — A5 segfault validation
pending.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests** — existing numerical comparisons
retained; no mock-only or text-matching tests added.
- [ ] **Performance impact** — no benchmark run; no performance
improvement claimed.

[CI] Upgrade selected test images to CANN 9.3.0 (#22151)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Switch the selected-tests container image registry to
`swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/atlas_inference/cann` and upgrade all
19 runner image tags from CANN 9.2.1 to `9.3.0_20261113161300`. Preserve
the hardware, card counts, OS/Python suffixes and csrc cache targets.

Also update the hardcoded CPU UT image tag in `pr_test.yaml` to
`9.3.0_20261113161300-910b-ubuntu22.04-py3.12`, since CPU UT supplies
its own test group instead of reading `runner_label.json`.

finally, update the timeout parameter for test case of eplb.

cases.

matches the CANN 9.3.0 runner tag.

the intended image-tag change; other runner metadata is unchanged.
- `git diff --check` passed for both changed files.
- `bash format.sh ci` could not run because `pre-commit` is not
installed.

require CI validation. No new runtime tests were added for this CI
configuration update.

update; runtime boundary, regression and performance tests do not apply.
- [ ] CI container pulls and NPU test validation completed.

[CI][Misc] Bump mooncake-transfer-engine-npu to 0.3.14.post1 (#23095)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Upgrade `mooncake-transfer-engine-npu` from `0.3.14` to `0.3.14.post1`
in the A2, A3, and A5 Docker images and in the PR and main2main CI
workflows. Update the dependency guide and its Chinese translation to
match.

Follow-up to #21834.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users of the affected Docker images will get Mooncake NPU
`0.3.14.post1` preinstalled.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed.
- Verified that all 10 files from #21834 contain only the intended
version substitutions.
- Confirmed that PyPI lists the `0.3.14.post1` ARM64 wheel for CPython
3.12.
- `bash format.sh ci` could not run because `pre-commit` is unavailable
locally.
- CI testing only for image builds, wheel installs, and Ascend NPU smoke
tests.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+# Step-5-Preview

+## 1 Introduction {: #1-introduction }
 
-**Step-5-Preview** is a next-generation flagship Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model developed by StepFun. The model has **600B** total parameters, with **27B** active per token, and supports a 1M-token context window and vision input.
+!!! note
 
-This document describes how to quickly get started with `Step-5-Preview` model inference deployment on Ascend NPU using vLLM-Ascend, based on W8A8 quantized weights.
+    The "PD Separation Deployment" mentioned in this document is provided only as an example/reference design to demonstrate the basic process of deploying Prefill and Decode in separated mode. It is not recommended for use in the production environment.
 
-!!! warning
+    **For the production environment on the customer side, [MindIE Motor](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/en/mindie/latest/quickstart/docs/en/user_guide/quick_start.md) + vLLM Ascend is recommended.**
 
-    **Current status and constraints**
+**Step-5-Preview** is a next-generation flagship Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model
+developed by StepFun. It has **600B** total parameters with **27B** active per
+token, supports a **1M-token** context window and vision input, and is validated
+only on **950DT products** (96GB × 8 per node). Other Ascend hardware, such as
+the A3 series, is not supported for `Step-5-Preview`.
 
-    - `Step-5-Preview` is provided **out-of-the-box** through the official Docker image `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:step5-a5-openeuler`. The supporting code has **not yet been merged** into the vLLM-Ascend repository, so installing it from source (`pip install` or building from source) is **not supported** for this model yet.
-    - Only **950DT products** are supported for this experimental release. Other Ascend hardware (e.g., Atlas A3 Products) is not supported for `Step-5-Preview`.
-    - The features listed in [Supported Features](#2-supported-features) are only those enabled by the verified deployment commands in this document, and do **not** imply that all features are supported for `Step-5-Preview`. This is an early-access version; performance optimization and reliability validation are still in progress (see [Declaration](#102-declaration)).
+This document shows the main verification steps of the model, including
+supported features, prerequisites, installation, online service deployment,
+functional verification, accuracy and performance evaluation, performance
+tuning, and FAQs.
 
-This document is written based on the custom vLLM Ascend Docker image built on v0.27.0. The supported runtime versions are listed in [Hardware and Software Preparation](#32-hardware-and-software-preparation). The model is supported only in the experimental configuration described in this guide.
+This guide covers two deployment scenarios on 950DT products:
 
-## 2 Supported Features
+- **Multi-node co-located deployment**: two nodes, with Prefill and Decode
+  running in one DP group, targeting the full 1M-token context.
+- **Prefill-Decode (PD) separation deployment**: six nodes (2 Prefill + 4
+  Decode), with an optional KV cache pool for prefix reuse.

+Together, the deployment examples in this document exercise tensor parallelism
+(TP), pipeline parallelism (PP), expert parallelism (EP), data parallelism (DP),
+native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding with three tokens, decode graph capture,
+shared-expert data parallelism, shared-expert overlap, and FlashComm1. Each
+topology in [Section 5](#5-online-service-deployment) enables the subset listed
+there: Prefill uses TP with PP, Decode uses TP with DP, and only the Decode role
+captures the decode graph. The PD examples additionally enable Prefill-Decode

+## 5 Online Service Deployment {: #5-online-service-deployment }
+
+This chapter covers the two supported topologies: multi-node co-located
+deployment and multi-node PD separation, the latter with an optional KV cache
+pool. Set the model path as described in [Section 3.1](#31-model-weight), and
+use the values of the selected role script. Hardware-specific and role-specific
+values are not interchangeable between Prefill and Decode.
+
+### 5.1 Multi-Node Co-located Deployment {: #51-multi-node-co-located-deployment }
+
+The validated co-located deployment uses two 950DT product nodes with eight devices
+per node. vLLM data parallelism spans the two nodes with two DP ranks per node,
+and tensor parallelism uses four devices in each rank, so the resulting topology
+is DP4/TP4/EP16. Prefill and Decode share the same engine and the same DP group,
+and the combined context limit is 1048576 tokens.
+
+Before starting the service:
+
+- Set `MODEL_PATH` to the container-visible checkpoint directory recorded in
+  [Section 3.1](#31-model-weight).
+- Set `NODE0_IP`, `NODE1_IP`, and `NIC_NAME` to each node's service IP and the
+  local network interface. Set `HCCL_IF_IP` to the communication IP owned by
+  that interface; use the same value as the service IP when the two are equal.
+  `--host` always binds the service IP.
+- Start Node 0 first, then start Node 1 as soon as possible. On Node 1,
+  `NODE0_IP` must equal `LOCAL_IP` on Node 0.
+- Node 1 joins the DP group as a headless worker with
+  `--data-parallel-start-rank 2`. The group runs two local ranks per node, so
+  rank `2` is the first global rank owned by the second node.
+
+Run the following script on each node. Select the tab for the node:
+
+=== "Node 0"
+
+    ```bash
+    export MODEL_PATH=<MODEL_PATH>
+    export NODE0_IP=<P0_IP>
+    export NODE1_IP=<P1_IP>
+    export NIC_NAME=<NIC_NAME>
+    LOCAL_IP="${NODE0_IP}"
+    export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1
+
+    unset http_proxy https_proxy ftp_proxy all_proxy
+    unset HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY FTP_PROXY ALL_PROXY
+
+    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
+    export HCCL_IF_IP=<NODE0_NIC_IP>
+    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=CCU_MS
+    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC_NAME}"
+    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC_NAME}"
+    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
+
+    vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
+        --host "${LOCAL_IP}" \
+        --port 7778 \
+        --served-model-name step \
+        --trust-remote-code \
+        --max-num-seqs 256 \
+        --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+        --max-model-len 1048576 \
+        --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+        --data-parallel-size 4 \
+        --data-parallel-size-local 2 \
+        --data-parallel-address "${NODE0_IP}" \
+        --data-parallel-rpc-port 13389 \
+        --enable-expert-parallel \
+        --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+        --prefix-cache-retention-interval 2048 \
+        --distributed-executor-backend "mp" \
+        --allowed-local-media-path / \
+        --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
+        --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true, "enable_shared_expert_dp": true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}' \
+        --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 3, "method": "mtp"}' \
+        --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+        --tool-call-parser step5 \
+        --reasoning-parser step5
+    ```
+
+=== "Node 1"
+
+    ```bash
+    export MODEL_PATH=<MODEL_PATH>
+    export NODE0_IP=<P0_IP>
+    export NODE1_IP=<P1_IP>
+    export NIC_NAME=<NIC_NAME>
+    LOCAL_IP="${NODE1_IP}"
+    export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1
+
+    unset http_proxy https_proxy ftp_proxy all_proxy
+    unset HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY FTP_PROXY ALL_PROXY
+
+    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
+    export HCCL_IF_IP=<NODE1_NIC_IP>
+    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=CCU_MS
+    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC_NAME}"
+    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC_NAME}"
+    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
+
+    vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
+        --host "${LOCAL_IP}" \
+        --port 7778 \
+        --served-model-name step \
+        --trust-remote-code \
+        --max-num-seqs 256 \
+        --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+        --max-model-len 1048576 \
+        --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+        --data-parallel-size 4 \
+        --data-parallel-size-local 2 \
+        --data-parallel-address "${NODE0_IP}" \
+        --headless \
+        --data-parallel-start-rank 2 \
+        --data-parallel-rpc-port 13389 \
+        --enable-expert-parallel \
+        --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+        --distributed-executor-backend "mp" \
+        --allowed-local-media-path / \
+        --prefix-cache-retention-interval 2048 \
+        --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
+        --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true, "enable_shared_expert_dp": true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}' \
+        --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 3, "method": "mtp"}' \
+        --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+        --tool-call-parser step5 \
+        --reasoning-parser step5
+    ```
+
+The following values differ between the master and the worker node:
+
+| Setting | Node 0 | Node 1 | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `LOCAL_IP` | Node 0 IP | Node 1 IP | Each node uses its own service IP. |
+| `NODE0_IP` | Not required | Node 0 IP | The worker uses this address to join the DP group. |
+| `--headless` | Omitted | Enabled | The worker does not expose an API endpoint. |
+| `--data-parallel-address` | `${NODE0_IP}` | `${NODE0_IP}` | Always resolves to Node 0. |
+| `--data-parallel-start-rank` | `0` (default) | `2` | First global rank owned by the node; every node needs a unique value. |
+
+Key multi-node co-located deployment parameters:
+
+| Parameter | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `--tensor-parallel-size 4` | Uses four NPUs per DP rank. |
+| `--data-parallel-size 4` | Creates four global DP ranks across the two nodes. |
+| `--data-parallel-size-local 2` | Runs two DP ranks per node, so all eight devices are in use with TP4. |
+| `--enable-expert-parallel` | Shards MoE experts across the DP and TP domains, giving EP16. |
+| `--max-model-len 1048576` | Combined input and output limit. |
+| `--max-num-seqs 256`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` | Per-engine scheduler limits. |
+| `--compilation-config` | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graph replay for decode. |
+| `--additional-config` | Enables FlashComm1, shared-expert data parallelism, and shared-expert overlap. |
+| `--speculative-config` | Native MTP decoding with three speculative tokens. |
+| `--enable-auto-tool-choice`, `--tool-call-parser step5` | Enables tool calling and parses Step-5's native tool-call format into standard `tool_calls`; without them `tools` requests are ignored. |
+| `--reasoning-parser step5` | Splits the output at Step-5's thinking markers, returning the chain of thought in `reasoning_content` instead of mixing it into `content`. |
+| `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` | Replaces the default Hugging Face tokenizer backend with the [fastokens](https://github.com/crusoecloud/fastokens) Rust implementation, which is faster on long prompts. Install `fastokens` (version 0.2.0 or later) in the same Python environment and check `python -c "import fastokens"`; with the variable set and the package missing, the engine stops at startup. Only the API server process on Node 0 builds a tokenizer, so the variable has no effect on the headless worker. |
+
+Because the weights are large, the load time is related to the disk read speed, and the first load usually takes about 10 minutes. After both nodes have joined and node 0 reports `Application startup complete`, the service is ready; see [Section 6](#6-functional-verification) for verification.
+
+### 5.2 Multi-Node PD Separation Deployment (2P4D) {: #52-multi-node-pd-separation-deployment-2p4d }
+
+The quantized model `Step-5-Preview-w8a8-mxfp8` is deployed on six 950DT
+products (96GB × 8 per node). Prefill runs as one DP1/TP4/PP4 engine across P0–P1,
+and Decode runs as one DP8/TP4 group across D0–D3 with two DP ranks per node.
+Both roles enable expert parallelism, and a Proxy forwards client requests to
+both roles.
+
+The parallelism layout, `--max-model-len`, and the scheduler limits in this
+section come from the validated Prefill and Decode scripts. Both roles use
+`--max-model-len 1048576` and `--max-num-seqs 256`; Prefill uses
+`--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` and Decode uses `2048`.
+
+Before starting the service:
+
+- Set `MODEL_PATH` to the container-visible checkpoint directory recorded in
+  [Section 3.1](#31-model-weight).
+- Set the IP and NIC variables to each node's service IP, its communication IP,
+  and the local interface that owns the communication IP.
+- Start P0 before P1, and D0 before D1–D3. Every Prefill node uses the same
+  master address and port; every Decode node uses the same DP address and DP RPC
+  port.
+- Only P0 and D0 expose the HTTP API. P1 and D1–D3 are headless workers, and
+  every worker needs a unique node rank or DP start rank.
+
+| Role | Nodes | DP | TP | PP | EP | Context limit | HTTP API |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Prefill | P0–P1 (2) | 1 | 4 | 4 | EP16 | 1048576 | P0 only |
+| Decode | D0–D3 (4) | 8 | 4 | 1 | EP32 | 1048576 | D0 only |
+| Proxy | One node (P0 in the reference run) | — | — | — | — | — | `<PROXY_PORT>` |
+| MetaService | One node, co-located with P0 in the reference run ([Section 5.3](#53-pd-separation-with-kv-cache-pool) only) | — | — | — | — | — | `8000` (metrics) |
+
+Use the same checkpoint revision, tokenizer, and quantization metadata on every
+node. Two addresses matter on each node: `LOCAL_IP` is the service IP that
+`--host` binds and that clients and the Proxy use, and `HCCL_IF_IP` is the
+communication IP owned by `NIC_NAME`. Keep them separate when the cluster has a
+service network and a compute network. Make sure every node can reach the
+Prefill, Decode, and Proxy service IPs.
+
+| Port or address | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `<P0_IP>`, `<P1_IP>` | Prefill node service IPs |
+| `<D0_IP>`–`<D3_IP>` | Decode node service IPs |
+| `<PROXY_IP>` | Proxy node IP |
+| `7778` | Prefill and Decode HTTP API port; only P0 and D0 expose it |
+| `7060` | Prefill pipeline master port |
+| `13389` | Decode DP RPC port |
+| `48100` | Prefill KV transfer base port (`kv_producer`) |
+| `48200` | Decode KV transfer base port (`kv_consumer`) |
+| `<PROXY_PORT>` | Proxy HTTP API port, chosen by the operator |
+
+#### 5.2.1 Create the Engine Templates {: #521-create-the-engine-templates }
+
+Save `run_p.sh` on both Prefill nodes and `run_d.sh` on all four Decode nodes.
+Select the tab for the role:

+=== "Prefill"

+    pipeline master and exposes the HTTP API; P1 joins as a headless worker.
+    `kv_port` is a base address: each engine rank listens on `kv_port + rank`, so
+    the 16 Prefill ranks need 16 consecutive ports and the 32 Decode ranks need
+    32. Keep both base ports outside the Mooncake-reserved `20000–27999` range;
+    the examples use `48100` and `48200`, which keeps the two ranges disjoint.

+#### 5.2.2 Start the Engines {: #522-start-the-engines }
+
+Start P0, then P1, then D0–D3, and finally the Proxy in
+[Section 5.2.3](#523-proxy). Start each coordinator first and bring up the
+remaining nodes immediately afterward, otherwise a worker can hit the
+engine-ready timeout.
+
+Wait for `Application startup complete` in the P0 and D0 logs, then check both
+APIs before starting the Proxy:
+
+```bash
+curl --noproxy '*' --fail --silent --show-error --output /dev/null \
+    --write-out '%{http_code}' "http://<P0_IP>:7778/health"; echo
+curl --noproxy '*' --fail --silent --show-error --output /dev/null \
+    --write-out '%{http_code}' "http://<D0_IP>:7778/health"; echo
+```
+
+Expected result: `200` from both. The Proxy has no `/health` route, so verify the
+full chain with a request through it as described in
+[Section 6.1](#61-text-requests); the KV path is working when Prefill logs the
+block save for that request and Decode logs the matching load. If either check
+fails, read the P0 and D0 logs and follow [Section 10](#10-faq).
+

+Both roles declare `kv_connector_extra_config` with the **global** Prefill and Decode topology, not the local node: Prefill is one DP1/TP4/PP4 engine and Decode is one DP8/TP4 group. Keep the same block on every node of a group.
+
+Prefill prioritizes TTFT, so it uses a larger batch-token budget and no graph capture; Decode prioritizes TPOT, so it captures the decode graph and uses a smaller batch-token budget. The setting is process-scoped: it applies to the process that builds the tokenizer, which is the API server on P0 and D0, and it has no effect on the headless nodes. Decode also tokenizes the prompt — the Proxy forwards the original chat request, and the KV transfer carries block ids only, not token ids — so keep the setting identical on both roles.

+Tool calling and reasoning output are parsed inside the API server that returns the response (D0 here; P0 for symmetry). -- The current version is only for early experience, and performance optimization is still in progress.
-- The service reliability has not been fully validated, and it is not recommended for direct use in production environments.
+- **Q: The service fails to start, or reports an out-of-memory error soon after accepting requests.**
+A: The scheduler limits, context length, or graph capture do not fit device memory. Lower `--max-num-seqs` or `--max-num-batched-tokens` first, then `--max-model-len` or `--gpu-memory-utilization`. On Decode, DP8 × TP4 can report `No available memory for the cache blocks`; keep the four-node group and cut the context or batch-token budget first, or fall back to TP8.
+- **Q: The pool hit rate is low or TTFT does not improve.**
+A: Shared prefixes must be block-aligned (the reference runs use multiples of 4096 tokens); a prefix that ends mid-block is never stored. Restart the engines between two identical measurements and read per-request metrics, not the cumulative counter. A 16k-token prefix occupies about 3.75 GiB per rank, so size `dram.size` per rank.
+- **Q: With the pool enabled, are prefix hits still served from local HBM?**
+A: Yes. `--enable-prefix-caching` stays on and `enable_lookup: true` makes each engine query the pool only for the blocks that miss in local HBM, so HBM is the first tier and the DRAM pool the second.
+- **Q: The Proxy hangs or stops forwarding.**
+A: A single-worker Proxy is blocked by one unfinished streaming handler. Restart the Proxy after any engine restart, and use non-streaming requests for load tests. A `JSONDecodeError` in the Proxy log means a backend returned an empty body or an HTML error page.

[Feature] Support fine-grained prefix matching and recovery for AscendStore (#21167)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

AscendStore bulk transfers support external prefix recovery at
Core-resolved `--prefix-match-unit` boundaries inside physical KV cache
pages.

- Use exact Store hash keys and Core's cache managers to find a common
recoverable prefix across Attention and Mamba groups, accounting for the
local HBM prefix and speculative replay.
- Pass each group's tail key to both load paths. Restore physical
Attention pages and exact Mamba checkpoints.
- Pin the checkpoint blocks handed off by Core until bulk save
completes. For roles that require EAGLE replay, all Mamba groups follow
the scheduler's common checkpoint boundary.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. AscendStore bulk pooling can reuse a cached prefix within a
physical KV page at the configured `--prefix-match-unit` boundaries. See
the [release note
fragment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/9368c8ba7a1fc7d606bc400773056ccdc9e50937/release_notes/fragments/21167.yaml).

### How was this patch tested?

NPU validation used Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at `9368c8b` with vLLM Core
`4ba787e`, MRv2, ACL graphs, MTP, and APC. The tables use
`--prefix-match-unit 64`.

| Deployment | HBM-only hit tokens | External-only hit tokens | Exact
cold-output match at hit lengths |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed TP2/DP1 | 2,112 / 2,176 / 2,240 | 2,112 / 2,176 / 2,240 | 2,176
/ 2,240 |
| PD TP2/DP1 per role | 2,112 / 2,176 / 2,240 | 2,112 / 2,176 / 2,240 |
2,112 |

| Deployment | HBM-only hit tokens | External-only hit tokens | Exact
