[Performance][PCP] Overlap local Q projection with global cache preparation (#21414)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DSA PCP prefill currently runs three things serially per layer:
gather/restore the hidden states, prepare the replicated caches (global
collectives), and only then compute the local Q prolog. The Q prolog
only reads local inputs and weights, so it can be issued on the
auxiliary stream while the caller stream performs the unchanged
collectives, hiding the Q cost behind communication.

This PR enables that overlap for PCP prefill on the existing DSA
multistream switch. No new configuration option is added:

- `_prepare_caches_and_query` replaces
`_prepare_caches_before_attention`: it prepares the caches and
optionally returns the Q intermediates produced by this invocation. The
base `AscendDSAImpl` implementation returns `(False, None)`, so non-PCP
behavior is untouched.
- `AscendDSAPCPImpl.__init__` maps the inherited
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` value into `pcp_q_projection_overlap` and
then sets the inherited flag to `False`, because PCP has already
prepared the replicated caches before local attention and must not start
a second cache-update overlap on the base path.
- `AscendDSAPCPImpl._prepare_caches_and_query` issues
`_mla_prolog_single_stream` on the existing overlap stream
(`dsv4_dsa_overlap_stream()`) for layers whose PCP metadata has a global
prefill and whose local query shard is nonempty. Every collective stays
on the caller stream in its original order, empty local shards still
join all collectives and skip the Q prolog, and the Q stream is joined
in a `finally` block so a failure cannot leave an unsynchronized stream.
- `AscendDSAImpl.forward` / `_forward_attention` consume the
invocation-local `prepared_query` instead of recomputing the prolog;
nothing is cached on the layer.
- Unit tests in `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_cp.py` and
`tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py` cover the config mapping, the
collective/stream ordering, and the failure-path join.

Serving behavior changes for PCP prefill: the overlap is on whenever
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` is enabled, which is the documented
default (`True`).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, but there is no new switch: PCP prefill Q-projection overlap is
controlled by the pre-existing `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap`
`additional-config` option (`vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`, default
`True`). A PCP deployment therefore gets the overlap without any extra
flag, and `--additional-config '{"multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap":
false}'` restores the serial gather-then-Q order.

Docs and release notes shipped in this PR:

- `docs/source/user_guide/configuration/additional_config.md`: the
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` row now also documents the PCP prefill
behavior and how to turn it off.
- `release_notes/fragments/21414.yaml`:

```yaml
pr: 21414
entries:
  - category: performance
    text: >-
      PCP prefill now overlaps the local Q projection with global cache
      preparation for nonempty local query shards, controlled by the existing
      `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` option (enabled by default). To run the
      two steps serially, launch with
      `--additional-config '{"multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap": false}'`.
```

### How was this patch tested?

#### 1. Unit tests (added in this PR)

`tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_cp.py` (+133) and
`tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py` (+20/-9) mock the NPU stream and
operator calls, so they need no NPU:

- `test_pcp_query_overlap_honors_config[False/True]`: `AscendDSAPCPImpl`
maps the inherited `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` value into
`pcp_q_projection_overlap` and leaves the inherited cache-update overlap
disabled.
- `test_cache_query_preparation_preserves_collectives` (12 cases:
overlap on/off x global-prefill/local-tokens x `compress_ratio`
1/4/128): asserts the Q prolog runs on the overlap stream only when
overlap is enabled, a global prefill exists and the local shard is
nonempty; the recorded call order is `query_wait, query, gather, swa[,
compressor][, indexer], weights, current_wait` for the overlapped cases
and the plain collective order otherwise, with no stream access at all
when overlap is off.
- `test_cache_query_preparation_joins_stream_on_failure` (7 injected
failure stages): the Q stream is still joined and the join is the last
stream operation.
- `test_cache_query_preparation_delegates_ordinary_metadata`: non-PCP
metadata falls back to the base implementation without touching any
stream or collective.
- `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py`: `_make_impl`/`_forward_attention`
call sites are updated for the new `prepared_query` plumbing, including
the `prepared_query`-first branch that skips `_mla_prolog_multistream`.

#### 2. NPU microbenchmark (8x Ascend 910B3, TP1 + PCP8)

Measured with an out-of-tree harness during development of this PR (the
comparison script itself is not part of the final diff; raw records live
outside the repo). Synthetic deterministic weights, BF16 Q down
projection and W8A8 Q up projection, seven alternating-order rounds of
50 executions per case, slowest rank's wall time, round median. Graph
mode (captured graphs, input values and RoPE buffers refreshed at fixed
addresses before each replay):

| tokens/rank | case | serial (ms) | overlap (ms) | delta |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | balanced | 1138.5 | 877.7 | -22.9% |
| 512 | balanced | 583.2 | 459.6 | -21.2% |
| 128 | balanced | 225.0 | 170.1 | -24.4% |
| 128 | uneven | 225.5 | 173.6 | -23.0% |
| 128 | strided input | 247.5 | 190.4 | -23.1% |
| 128 | empty rank | 225.4 | 170.4 | -24.4% |
| 1 | all inputs empty | 32.4 | 33.0 | +1.8% |

Eager mode is slower with the extra stream context (1089.8 ms -> 1395.4
ms at 1024 tokens/rank), so the win is claimed for graph execution only.
The degenerate all-empty case has nothing to overlap and stays within
noise.

This slowdown is specific to the **eager overlap implementation in the Q
+ gather microbenchmark**; it does not imply that an entire eager model
or PIECEWISE service is slower. Full-model execution includes
inter-layer pipelining, and profiling of continuous PIECEWISE execution
confirmed real Q/communication overlap. The microbenchmark regression
can therefore coexist with the **+2.1% end-to-end output throughput
improvement** observed in the three-round serving A/B below.

#### 3. Communication overlap profile (1024 tokens/rank, 20 replays)

| metric | serial | overlap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| span | 22.63 ms | 17.35 ms |
| compute union | 12.87 ms | 17.16 ms |
| communication union | 9.58 ms | 10.69 ms |
| overlapped communication | 0 us | 10.67 ms |
| idle | 182 us | 159 us |

#### 4. Correctness parity of the overlapped schedule

The same harness compared both paths against independently constructed
CPU reference tensors over 56 rank-cases and 504 comparison groups (1701
non-empty tensor comparisons) in `eager`, `serial_graph`, and
`overlap_graph` phases, covering uneven lengths, an empty rank,
all-empty logical input, noncontiguous input, and graph replays with
refreshed values:

- all 1701 tensor comparisons bitwise equal (`max_abs = 0`, relative L2
= 0);
- restoration indices compared exactly;
- no phase reported a failure.

This is a kernel-level parity check of the overlapped schedule, not a
model accuracy evaluation.

#### 5. End-to-end serving validation (DeepSeek V4 Flash PD)

2 prefill + 2 decode workers, 32 concurrency, 667 streaming requests per
round, 3 baseline rounds followed by 3 candidate rounds on the same
deployment. These rounds were collected before the switch was
consolidated onto `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap`; the overlapped
schedule they measure is the one in this PR. 9/9 smoke cases pass in
both phases, and every round reported 667/667 successful requests with 0
failures.

| metric (median of 3 rounds) | baseline | candidate | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Avg TTFT (ms) | 19520.95 | 19068.62 | -2.3% |
| Avg TPOT (ms) | 12.25 | 12.21 | -0.3% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 930.92 | 950.88 | +2.1% |
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 119414.04 | 121979.34 | +2.1% |
| Avg latency (s) | 31.95 | 31.68 | -0.8% |

That workload is queue-dominated (prefill queue ratio ~0.89, ~1.5 s of
prefill compute against ~13 s of queue time), so the end-to-end delta is
close to run-to-run noise; it is not claimed as a serving-level win. The
microbenchmark and the profile above are the evidence for the
layer-level overlap, and an end-to-end gain needs a prefill-bound
workload.

#### 6. Lint

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0, the version pinned
in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) pass on the touched Python files.

### Checklist

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the overlap is gated on a
global prefill plus a nonempty local query shard; empty shards keep
participating in every collective, and non-PCP metadata delegates to the
base implementation. Unit tests cover all 12 gate/compression
combinations.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not applicable, this is not a bug fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the Q stream join is in a
`finally` block and
`test_cache_query_preparation_joins_stream_on_failure` injects a failure
at each stage to assert the join still happens.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: unit tests assert the exact
stream/collective call order, and the out-of-tree harness compared both
paths against independent CPU reference tensors with bitwise equality.
- [x] **Performance impact**: microbenchmark and profile results are
attached above; the overlap rides on the existing
`multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` default and can be disabled with the same
option.

[Doc] Add PD disaggregation guide for Qwen3.8-27B (#23070)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregation deployment guidance to the
Qwen3.8-27B tutorial, which previously only covered single-node online
deployment:

- **Section 5.2 (Atlas 800I A3)**: 3P1D single-host layout on 16 NPUs,
TP2 per group, with complete Prefill/Decode/proxy scripts and key
parameter descriptions (P:D ratio guidance, per-role
`--max-num-batched-tokens`/`--max-num-seqs` tuning, hybrid-attention
`--mamba-cache-mode align` requirement for prefix caching,
`gdn_prefill_backend: fla_npu`, `engine_id` uniqueness).
- **Section 5.3 (950PR&950DT Products)**: 4P1D single-host,
single-NPU-per-group (DP-first) layout with C8 (`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`
+ w8a8c8 checkpoint), covering prefill/decode scripts, proxy, and C8
requirements.
- **Section 5.4 (Request Forwarding)**: connector-proxy pairing and
troubleshooting path.
- Introduction updated to mention the new PD disaggregation sections.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes - documentation only. New PD disaggregation recipes for Qwen3.8-27B
on A3 and 950PR&950DT.

## How was this patch tested?

- Docs build / markdown lint checked locally (remaining markdownlint
warnings are pre-existing on main).
- Deployment commands are adapted from validated internal SR deployment
recipes (A3: TP2 3P1D; 950-series: TP1 4P1D with C8). CI testing only
for hardware coverage.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: 周祎璠 <zhouyifan29@huawei.com>
Co-authored-by: 周祎璠 <zhouyifan29@huawei.com>

-## 6 Functional Verification
+### 5.2 Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (Atlas 800I A3) {: #52-prefill-decode-disaggregation-atlas-800i-a3 }
+
+PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. Prefill groups process large prompt chunks with a large `--max-num-batched-tokens` in eager mode; Decode groups serve token generation with a small `--max-num-batched-tokens`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` aclgraph, and the recompute scheduler. A Pull proxy forwards each request to Prefill first and then to Decode, and Decode pulls the KV cache from Prefill through Mooncake.
+
+The launch scripts below tune kernel parameters with `sysctl`. This requires `root` **and** write permission on `/proc/sys` — inside a container, being `root` (`id -u` returning `0`) is not sufficient by default: a non-privileged container mounts `/proc/sys` read-only. Use a privileged container (`--privileged`), or configure these kernel parameters on the host beforehand. Verify with a dry-run write before starting:
+
+```shell
+id -u          # must print 0 for root
+sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 && echo OK   # dry-run the write permission; "OK" means /proc/sys is writable
+```
+
+The scripts run under `set -euo pipefail`; a `sysctl` call that fails (for example `kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns`, which the EEVDF scheduler removed in Linux 6.6+) aborts the launch, so the scripts guard each tuning call with `|| true`.
+
+This example deploys **3P1D on one 16-NPU Atlas 800I A3 host** for the 64K-input / 1K-output workload with a 0% prefix-cache hit rate. Each service group uses TP2 on 2 NPUs. "3P1D" describes four service groups; it does not mean that P and D must occupy separate hosts.
+
+| Service group | Physical devices | TP | DP | HTTP port | Mooncake KV port | `engine_id` |
+|---------------|------------------|----|----|-----------|------------------|-------------|
+| Prefill P0    | 8,9              | 2  | 1  | 8081      | 58010            | 0           |
+| Prefill P1    | 10,11            | 2  | 1  | 8082      | 58020            | 1           |
+| Prefill P2    | 12,13            | 2  | 1  | 8083      | 58030            | 2           |
+| Decode D0     | 14,15            | 2  | 1  | 8088      | 58080            | 7           |
+
+We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md) for the general PD disaggregation workflow. This example uses `MooncakeConnectorV1` with the standard Pull proxy in [Section 5.4](#54-request-forwarding).
+
+#### 5.2.1 Prefill Service Group
+
+Create `run_p.sh` on the A3 host. P0, P1, and P2 use the same script with different `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, HTTP port, Mooncake `kv_port`, and `engine_id`. The values below are for P0.
+
+```shell
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+unset ftp_proxy
+unset https_proxy
+unset http_proxy
+
+MODEL_PATH="<LOCAL_W8A8_MODEL_PATH>"   # e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8
+
+export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=8,9
+export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True"
+export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
+sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 || true
+sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 || true
+sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 || true  # no-op on EEVDF (Linux 6.6+), which removed this parameter
+export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2
+
+# HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV" is only used on the Decode side; unset any
+# value inherited from a previous Decode/co-located session in this terminal,
+# otherwise long-input Prefill slows down.
+unset HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE
+
+# Single-host deployment; use the host service IP for multi-host deployment
+export HCCL_IF_IP="127.0.0.1"
+export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512
+export ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL="0:0"
+# e.g. enp48s3u1u1; find the active NIC with "ip a" (do not use "lo",
+# or Mooncake transfer setup fails)
+export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="<SERVICE_NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
+export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/python/site-packages/mooncake:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
+
+vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --port 8081 \
+    --data-parallel-size 1 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --served-model-name "qwen3.8" \
+    --max-model-len 133120 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 66000 \
+    --max-num-seqs 8 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --quantization ascend \
+    --enforce-eager \
+    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
+    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true}' \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{
+        "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV1",
+        "kv_buffer_device": "npu",
+        "kv_role": "kv_producer",
+        "kv_port": "58010",
+        "engine_id": "0",
+        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+            "prefill": {"dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 2},
+            "decode":  {"dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 2}
+        }
+    }'
+```
+
+Run the script once per Prefill group in separate terminals:
+
+```shell
+bash run_p.sh   # P0; repeat with P1/P2 values for the other two groups
+```
+
+If a Prefill service does not become ready, confirm that its two devices are free, and that its HTTP port and Mooncake KV port are unused.
+

+```shell

+    --decoder-ports 8088
+```
+
+Send client requests to `http://<HOST_IP>:8199`.
+
+**Key Parameter Descriptions:**
+
+The P:D group ratio and the parameter values in the two scripts should be adapted to the workload:
+
+- The P:D group ratio follows the workload. Workloads dominated by long, uncached inputs (e.g., long-context summarization over unique documents) need more Prefill groups; workloads with a high prefix-cache hit rate spend most wall time in decode and shift capacity toward Decode (e.g., 1P2D).
+- On Prefill, `--max-num-batched-tokens` should be no smaller than the effective uncached input length (within the HBM activation budget), so a prompt is prefilled in a single chunk instead of being split into multiple rounds. The example uses `66000` for a 64K-token 0%-cache-hit input budget; scale it down when prefix caching absorbs most of the input, because a cold request of the full length can transiently exceed the activation budget and cause OOM.
+- `--max-num-seqs` on Prefill bounds concurrent prefill batches per group. Keep it small for long-input workloads so each chunk gets the full HBM activation budget; larger values are reasonable for short inputs.
+- Qwen3.8-27B is a hybrid-attention model: only 16 of 64 layers use full attention, and the other 48 Gated DeltaNet layers carry a recurrent state. To enable prefix caching in PD mode, replace `--no-enable-prefix-caching` with `--enable-prefix-caching` on P and D, and keep the choice identical on both roles; the recurrent-state cache is aligned with the KV blocks automatically, no extra flag is needed.
+- The FLA AscendC prefill kernel for the linear-attention layers is enabled automatically on hardware profiles that support it, so no extra configuration is needed for prefill throughput.
+- `HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"` is set only on Decode. Do not export it (directly or through a shared terminal) when launching Prefill; long-input prefill slows down with AIV.
+- Keep `--served-model-name`, the checkpoint, and the MTP `method`/`num_speculative_tokens` identical on P and D; change them only together.
+- On Decode, the `cudagraph_capture_sizes` are coupled to MTP: with `num_speculative_tokens = N`, each capture size must be a multiple of `N + 1` (the example uses `4`-multiples for `num_speculative_tokens = 3`). If you change `num_speculative_tokens` or disable MTP, regenerate the list accordingly (e.g., `N = 4` → `5, 10, 15, ...`); otherwise the actual decode batch size cannot hit a captured graph, aclgraph silently falls back to eager, and TPOT degrades.
+- `engine_id` must be unique across all services in the same PD cluster. Each service must also use its own HTTP port and Mooncake KV port.
+- If multiple PD deployments run on the same host, stagger their HTTP and Mooncake KV ports.
+
+### 5.3 Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (950PR&950DT Products) {: #53-prefill-decode-disaggregation-950pr950dt-products }
+
+This example deploys **4P1D on one 950-series host** with the `Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8` checkpoint and C8 (`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`). Each group is single-NPU TP1, following the DP-first principle for this model size. P1-P4 use the same script with different `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (0/1/2/3), HTTP port (9090/9092/9094/9096), Mooncake `kv_port` (58010/58020/58030/58040), and `engine_id` (3/4/5/6). The values below are for P1.
+
+| Service group | NPUs | TP | DP | HTTP port | Mooncake KV port | `engine_id` |
+| ------------- | ---- | -- | -- | --------- | ---------------- | ----------- |
+| Prefill P1-P4 | 0-3 | 1 | 1 | 9090/9092/9094/9096 | 58010/58020/58030/58040 | 3/4/5/6 |
+| Decode D | 4 | 1 | 1 | 10000 | 58080 | 2 |
+
+#### 5.3.1 Prefill Node
+
+```shell
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+unset ftp_proxy
+unset https_proxy
+unset http_proxy
+
+MODEL_PATH="<LOCAL_W8A8C8_MODEL_PATH>"   # e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8
+
+export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.3"}'
+export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
+export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True"
+export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
+sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 || true
+sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 || true
+sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 || true  # no-op on EEVDF (Linux 6.6+), which removed this parameter
+export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
+
+# Single-host deployment; use the host service IP for multi-host deployment
+export HCCL_IF_IP="127.0.0.1"
+export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AI_CPU"
+export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
+export ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL="0:0"
+# e.g. enp48s3u1u1; find the active NIC with "ip a" (do not use "lo",
+# or Mooncake transfer setup fails)
+export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="<SERVICE_NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
+
+vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
+    --served-model-name "qwen3.8" \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --port 9090 \
+    --data-parallel-size 1 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype mxfp8 \
+    --max-model-len 153600 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+    --max-num-seqs 32 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --quantization ascend \
+    --enforce-eager \
+    --allowed-local-media-path / \
+    --mm-processor-cache-gb 3 \
+    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
+    --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
+    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true}' \
+    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
+    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{
+        "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV1",
+        "kv_buffer_device": "npu",
+        "kv_role": "kv_producer",
+        "kv_port": "58010",
+        "engine_id": "3",
+        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+            "prefill": {"dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1},
+            "decode":  {"dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1}
+        }
+    }'
+```
+
+#### 5.3.2 Decode Node
+
+```shell
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+unset ftp_proxy
+unset https_proxy
+unset http_proxy
+
+MODEL_PATH="<LOCAL_W8A8C8_MODEL_PATH>"
+
+export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.3"}'
+export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4
+export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True"
+export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
+sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 || true
+sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 || true
+sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 || true  # no-op on EEVDF (Linux 6.6+), which removed this parameter
+export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
+
+export HCCL_IF_IP="127.0.0.1"
+export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AI_CPU"
+export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
+export ASCEND_BUFFER_POOL="0:0"
+# e.g. enp48s3u1u1; find the active NIC with "ip a" (do not use "lo",
+# or Mooncake transfer setup fails)
+export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="<SERVICE_NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
+
+vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
+    --served-model-name "qwen3.8" \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --port 10000 \
+    --data-parallel-size 1 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype mxfp8 \
+    --max-model-len 153600 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+    --max-num-seqs 64 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --quantization ascend \
+    --allowed-local-media-path / \
+    --mm-processor-cache-gb 3 \
+    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
+    --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
+    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,40,44,48,52,56,60,64,68,72,76,80,84,88,92,96,100,104,108,112,116,120,124,128,132,136,140,144,148,152,156,160,164,168,172,176,180,184,188,192,196,200,204,208,212,216,220,224,228,232,236,240,244,248,252,256], "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
+    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "scheduler_config": {"recompute_scheduler_enable": true}}' \
+    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
+    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{
+        "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV1",
+        "kv_buffer_device": "npu",
+        "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
+        "kv_port": "58080",
+        "engine_id": "2",
+        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+            "prefill": {"dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1},
+            "decode":  {"dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1}
+        }
+    }'
+```
+
+#### 5.3.3 Proxy
+
+After all services report ready, start the standard Pull proxy on the same host:
+
+```shell
+unset ftp_proxy
+unset https_proxy
+unset http_proxy
+
+python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
+    --port 8090 \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --prefiller-hosts 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 \
+    --prefiller-ports 9090 9092 9094 9096 \
+    --decoder-hosts 127.0.0.1 \
+    --decoder-ports 10000
+```
+
+Send client requests to `http://<HOST_IP>:8090`.
+
+**C8 requirements for PD:**
+
+- P and D must use the same checkpoint revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata, and `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`.
+- C8 (`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`) is supported on 950PR&950DT Products only. With it enabled, `--block-size` must be a multiple of 512 (it defaults to 512 if unset).
+- After the PD data path is up, check outputs for repeated punctuation or abnormal repetition, which indicate a KV-transfer or quantization mismatch.
+
+### 5.4 Request Forwarding {: #54-request-forwarding }
+
+Use the proxy paired with the actual connector, rather than choosing it by hardware name. The standard proxy script is in `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/`; run the command from that directory. Replace the example hosts with reachable service IPs and use each service's HTTP port. `--served-model-name` is a server-side CLI parameter configured identically when launching P and D; the client is not involved in configuring it, but each client request must set its `model` field to that same served-model name (for example `"model": "qwen3.8"` in the request body).
+
+| Connector | Request Order | Proxy | Scope |
+| --------- | ------------- | ----- | ----- |
+| `MooncakeConnectorV1` | Proxy calls P, then D; D pulls KV | `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py` | A3 and 950PR&950DT PD recipes in [Section 5.2](#52-prefill-decode-disaggregation-atlas-800i-a3) and [Section 5.3](#53-prefill-decode-disaggregation-950pr950dt-products) |
+
+Do not use a DP RPC port or a Mooncake KV-transfer port as a proxy backend. If requests reach the proxy but return no output, verify the P and D `/health` endpoints from the proxy host, confirm that the configured backend addresses exactly match each service's `--host` and HTTP port, and then run the end-to-end checks in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).
+
+## 6 Functional Verification {: #6-functional-verification }
 
 After the service is started, the model can be invoked by sending a prompt. Two API interfaces are supported: `completions` and `chat/completions`. Use the `--served-model-name` you configured (`qwen3.8` for `Qwen3.8-27B`).
 
@@ -529,7 +903,7 @@ Refer to [vllm benchmark](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/benchmarking/) for more
 >
 > **950PR&950DT Products**: The `Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8` model weight easily fits in a single NPU (96 GB HBM per NPU on 950DT Products, 128 GB on 950PR Products). Following the **DP-first** principle, **TP=1 is the recommended default** for most scenarios, and the remaining NPUs should be allocated to DP for parallel request batches. The C8 weights are recommended for long-sequence scenarios and are served with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`; for short-sequence scenarios (e.g., 16k input), use `Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-mxfp8` without `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. `--max-model-len` can support up to **262144** in the same TP=1 + DP=8 layout.

[Doc][Recipe] Add deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro Ascend recipe overlay (#22438)

## PR title

[Doc][Recipe] Add deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro Ascend recipe overlay

## Summary

Add an Atlas 800I A2 (910B4) W4A8 overlay for DeepSeek-V4-Pro: a
four-node
co-located pool, DP4 x TP8 with expert parallelism (EP32), one local DP
rank
per node over all eight devices.

## Model and precision matrix

| Model | Checkpoint | Precision | Hardware | Nodes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro | Eco-Tech/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-w4a8 | W4A8 (int4) |
ascend_910b | 4 |

## Deployment coverage

| Strategy | Status |
|---|---|
| multi_node_dep | **verified** (4 nodes, DP4/TP8) |
| single_node_tp / tep / dep | unsupported |
| multi_node_tp / tep / pd_cluster | unsupported |

## Changes

- New file: `recipes/overlays/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml`
- Adds `ascend_910b` hardware status, an `ascend_w4a8` variant, and a
  `multi_node_dep` preset for a four-node co-located pool
- No changes to any existing recipe

## Test evidence

### Static validation and rendering

node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm-ascend --dir <recipes
dir>
✓ vllm-ascend recipes are valid against the renderer

pnpm test:schema        pass 5   fail 0
pnpm test:overlay       pass 13  fail 0
pnpm test:presets       pass 15  fail 0
pnpm test:hardware      pass 22  fail 0
pnpm test:pd-connectors pass 24  fail 0
pnpm test:guide-html    pass 29  fail 0

`pnpm test:render` was not run locally (needs `sync-sources` which
requires
outbound network on the dev box); it runs in CI.

### NPU smoke and inference correctness

Four Atlas 800I A2 nodes, 8x Ascend 910B4 (64 GB) each,
image `quay.nju.edu.cn/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1`:

- All engines reached `Application startup complete`
- `/health` returned 200 on node 0 (the only API endpoint)
- Single completion request: **HTTP 200 in 55.8 s** (cold); repeat
request 1.4 s
- `1+1=?` with `max_tokens=200` returned content `"2"`
(finish_reason=stop)
- Eight concurrent requests: **8/8 returned 200**, total wall time 72 s
  (≈ one request, confirming the four DP ranks share the load)

### Multi-node distributed connectivity

All four nodes reachable on the NPU side (hccn_tool ping, full mesh, 0%
loss).
DP group formed: `All engine subscriptions received by DP coordinator`.

### Performance benchmarks

Not yet run. Planned with AISBench (tutorial §8).

### Fault tolerance and negative cases

Observed and documented in the hardware note:

- Without `--api-server-count 1` on node 0, vLLM defaults it to
`data_parallel_size` (4), starts four API servers binding ranks that
live on
  other hosts, and **every completion request hangs until timeout while
  `/health` still returns 200**.
- Without `--headless` on nodes 1-3, node 0 aborts with
`Remote engine N must use --headless unless in external or hybrid dp lb
mode`.

## Backward compatibility

New file only; no existing recipe is modified.

## Documentation

`runbook` and `hardware_notes` describe the topology, the two pre-launch
edits,
and the measured per-device footprint (37.72 GiB weights + 12.88 GiB KV
cache).

## Preview and merge checklist

- [x] Recipes CI green on final head
- [x] `recipe` label added
- [x] Preview deployment succeeds on final head

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

Signed-off-by: wlei1715 <279283324+wlei1715@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: 余伟 <318087827+johnyu2007428-cmyk@users.noreply.github.com>

+      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '10'
+    hardware_overrides:
+      ascend_910b:
+        docker_image: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1
+        docker_shm_size: "512g"
+        docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"
+        install:
+          pip: false
+
+presets:
+  ascend_a2_w4a8_multinode_dep:
+    label: Ascend A2 W4A8 multi-node DP4/TP8 (4 nodes)
+    hardware: ascend_910b
+    strategy: multi_node_dep
+    variants: [ascend_w4a8]
+    default: false
+    select:
+      # Co-located multi-node pool, not PD disaggregation: the node count is
+      # set by select.nodes, and pd_router / pd_connector are omitted because
+      # they only apply to pd_cluster.
+      nodes: 4
+      frontend: python
+      kv_offload: false
+      features:
+        # spec_decoding is carried by the variant's extra_args; enabling the
+        # base feature as well would emit a second --speculative-config.
+        spec_decoding: false
+    source:
+      label: vLLM Ascend DeepSeek-V4-Pro tutorial
+      href: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.html
+      key: dsv4pro-a2-w4a8-multinode-dep
+      revision: '2026-11-19'
+    runbook: |
+      ## Topology
+
+      Four Atlas 800I A2 nodes, eight Ascend 910B4 (64 GB) each, 32 devices in
+      total. Global parallelism is **DP4 / TP8**, and with
+      `--enable-expert-parallel` the expert-parallel size is **EP32**
+      (DP4 x TP8). Every node carries exactly one local DP rank spanning all
+      eight devices; node 0 is the DP master and the only API endpoint.
+
+      Expert weights (733 GiB, 90% of the checkpoint) are sharded across all 32
+      devices — about 22.9 GiB of routed-expert weights per device. Attention,
+      embedding, lm_head and the DSpark/MTP draft layers are replicated once per
+      DP rank and sharded by TP inside the rank. Measured per-device footprint:
+      **37.72 GiB weights + 12.88 GiB KV cache**, i.e. 90% of 64 GB as set by
+      `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`.
+
+      ## Environment
+
+      Set the node IP and NIC per host. All four nodes must use the **same**
+      `--data-parallel-address` (node 0's service IP). The DP RPC port defaults
+      to 12321 and must be reachable between nodes.
+
+      Start node 0 first so the DP coordinator is listening, then nodes 1-3.
+
+      ## Launch order and flags
+
+      1. Node 0: no `--headless`, no `--data-parallel-start-rank`, **plus
+         `--api-server-count 1`**.
+      2. Nodes 1-3: `--headless` and `--data-parallel-start-rank 1|2|3`.
+
+      Omitting `--api-server-count 1` on node 0 is the most damaging mistake:
+      health checks pass while inference hangs. Always verify with a real
+      completion request, not just `/health`.
+    # No roles: schema roles only carry prefill / decode (pd_cluster
+    # semantics), while these four nodes form one group with no P/D split.
+    # Per-node differences are described in hardware_notes. The args and env
+    # below are the ones every node carries, matching the tested commands.
+    args:
+      # Topology is stated explicitly rather than left to the renderer. The
+      # multi_node_dep strategy defaults local DP to the whole node (8), which
+      # rendered DP32 / local8 with no TP for this recipe; the validated
+      # commands run DP4 / local1 / TP8 with one DP rank per node.
+      #
+      # Both flags have to live here rather than in `tp:` fields: a preset-level
+      # `tp` is only valid for single_node_tp (recipe-presets.js rejects any
+      # other strategy), and `variants.<key>.tp` does not reach a multi_node
+      # command at all. Global DP follows from node count x local DP.
+      - '--data-parallel-size-local'
+      - '1'
+      - '--tensor-parallel-size'
+      - '8'
+      - '--max-num-batched-tokens'
+      - '4096'
+      - '--max-num-seqs'
+      - '16'
+      - '--no-enable-prefix-caching'
+      - '--compilation-config'
+      - '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
+      - '--additional-config'
+      - '{"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":false},"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true,"enable_flashcomm1":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true}'
+    # The base recipe's base_args carry --kv-cache-dtype fp8 and the strategy
+    # adds --data-parallel-hybrid-lb; the validated W4A8 commands pass neither.
+    # Boolean flags like the hybrid-lb one can only be dropped, not negated by
+    # writing an opposite value.
+    remove_args:
+      - '--kv-cache-dtype'
+      - '--data-parallel-hybrid-lb'
+    env:
+      HCCL_IF_IP: $NODE_IP
+      VLLM_HOST_IP: $NODE_IP
+      HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+      GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+      TP_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME

[Doc][Recipe] add Ascend 910B (Atlas 800I A2) W4A8 PD support to Kimi-K2.7-Code overlay (#22726)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` overlay with validated **Ascend
910B** (Atlas 800I A2 / 910B4) support for the W4A8 checkpoint in
prefill/decode disaggregation, expressed with the generic PD pools
introduced in #1226.

Why: Kimi-K2.7-Code is a 1T-parameter coding MoE, and the Ascend W4A8
checkpoint fits a 2P+2D Atlas 800I A2 deployment, but the builder had no
selectable Ascend configuration for this model. The overlay makes the
qualified contract reproducible: two prefill nodes (DP2 x TP8), two
decode nodes (DP4 x TP4), `MooncakeConnectorV1` plus
`AscendStoreConnector` KV transfer, DFlash 15-token drafting, and the
Ascend proxy as the PD front end.

PD is the only supported strategy on 910B; the non-PD strategies are
marked unsupported.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Recipes metadata only (builder output for Huawei hardware on
recipes.vllm.ai); no vllm-ascend code, API, or runtime behaviour
changes.
No release note fragment.

### How was this patch tested?

1. **Real hardware**: 4 nodes x 8 NPU (32x Ascend 910B4, 64 GB HBM each)
with `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K2.7-Code-w4a8` (revision
`a671b826a7329495a89d6ff70b9c4ea96588c035`) and the Ascend proxy.
Topology: two prefill nodes DP2 x TP8, two decode nodes DP4 x TP4 (local
DP2 per node, ports 7100/7101), `MooncakeConnectorV1` +
`AscendStoreConnector` KV transfer, `z-lab/Kimi-K2.5-DFlash` with 15
speculative tokens. All six engine endpoints and the proxy returned HTTP
200.

- Base recipe:
`vllm-project/vllm@3b95523ed904cf02a26b872f4a900ef17e6be8ad`

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

Signed-off-by: troubadourHUI <s00491973@huawei.com>
Co-authored-by: troubadourHUI <s00491973@huawei.com>
Co-authored-by: 王磊 <279283324+wlei1715@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: 余伟 <318087827+johnyu2007428-cmyk@users.noreply.github.com>

new file mode 100644
@@ -0,0 +1,357 @@
+# Source: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code.yaml
+# Ascend overlay validated on 2 prefill + 2 decode Atlas 800I A2 nodes.
+meta:
+  date_updated: 2026-11-21
+  hardware:
+    ascend_910b: verified
+
+hardware_notes:
+  ascend_910b:
+    title: "Atlas 800I A2 (910B4) four-node PD"
+    body: |
+      Requires two prefill and two decode nodes, each with 8 x 64 GB NPUs.
+      Provide the model cache or weights path on every node, set
+      `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`, and start `mooncake_master` before the engines.
+      When using the rendered Docker command, add
+      `-v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf:ro`; the default mount set omits it.
+    link:
+      label: vLLM Ascend PD disaggregation guide
+      href: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html
+
+strategy_hardware:
+  single_node_tp:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  single_node_tep:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  single_node_dep:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  multi_node_tp:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  multi_node_tp_pp:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  multi_node_dep:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  multi_node_tep:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: unsupported
+  pd_cluster:
+    npu: unsupported
+    ascend_910b: supported
+
+# The validated lane uses four 8-device nodes: two prefill and two decode.
+strategy_min_gpus:
+  ascend_910b:
+    pd_cluster: 32
+
+features:
+  # The base recipe ships an Eagle3 draft. The Ascend lane was validated with
+  # the DFlash draft, which needs the Ascend dflash method and 15 draft tokens.
+  spec_decoding:
+    hardware_overrides:
+      ascend_910b:
+        args:
+          - '--speculative-config'
+          - '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Kimi-K2.5-DFlash","num_speculative_tokens":15}'
+
+variants:
+  ascend_w4a8:
+    model_id: Eco-Tech/Kimi-K2.7-Code-w4a8
+    precision: int4
+    label: W4A8 (Ascend A2)
+    vram_minimum_gb: 529
+    description: >-
+      ModelSlim INT4 W4A8 checkpoint for Atlas 800I A2 (910B4), served as a
+      two-node prefill pool (DP2 x TP8) and a two-node decode pool
+      (DP4 x TP4, two local DP ranks per node). Requires --quantization ascend.
+    supported_hardware:
+      - ascend_910b
+    min_vllm_version: '0.32.0'
+    extra_args:
+      - '--quantization'
+      - ascend
+      - '--host'
+      - 0.0.0.0
+      - '--served-model-name'
+      - kimi27
+      - '--seed'
+      - '1024'
+      - '--max-model-len'
+      - '71680'
+      - '--gpu-memory-utilization'
+      - '0.95'
+      - '--enable-prefix-caching'
+      - '--async-scheduling'
+      - '--mm-processor-cache-gb'
+      - '0'
+      - '--compilation-config'
+      - '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
+    extra_env:
+      PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF: expandable_segments:True
+      OMP_PROC_BIND: 'false'
+      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
+      TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE: '1'
+      VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT: '3600000'
+      HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE: AIV
+      HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE: '1'
+      ACL_OP_INIT_MODE: '1'
+      PYTHONHASHSEED: '0'
+      # Both the W4A8 checkpoint and the DFlash draft are published on
+      # ModelScope; resolve model ids there instead of Hugging Face.
+      VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE: 'true'
+      # The Mooncake-backed KV tiers read this path on every engine. Export the
+      # real path before launch; the runbook includes the shared config shape.
+      MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH: "$MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH"
+    hardware_overrides:
+      ascend_910b:
+        docker_image: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1
+        docker_shm_size: "1g"
+        docker_serve_command: "vllm serve"
+        install:
+          pip: false
+presets:
+  ascend_a2_w4a8_pd:
+    label: Ascend A2 W4A8 PD (2P + 2D)
+    hardware: ascend_910b
+    strategy: pd_cluster
+    variants: [ascend_w4a8]
+    default: true
+    select:
+      pd_router: ascend
+      pd_connector: mooncake_ascend
+      frontend: python
+      kv_offload: false
+      features:
+        spec_decoding: true
+        # The validated command does not pass --mm-encoder-tp-mode data.
+        encoder_parallel: false
+    source:
+      label: vLLM Ascend Mooncake multi-node PD guide
+      href: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html
+      key: kimi-k27-a2-w4a8-pd
+      revision: '2026-11-21'
+    description: >-
+      Two prefill nodes (DP2 x TP8) and two decode nodes (DP4 x TP4), with
+      Mooncake KV transfer and the Ascend proxy in front.
+    workload: 64k input / 1k output chat and agentic coding traffic.
+
+    image:
+      vllm: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1
+      model_revision: a671b826a7329495a89d6ff70b9c4ea96588c035
+
+    # The Ascend proxy uses external DP. The base recipe may leave a hybrid-LB
+    # flag behind; clear it so the rendered rank endpoints stay consistent.
+    remove_args: ["--data-parallel-hybrid-lb"]
+    roles:
+      prefill:
+        nodes: 2
+        parallelism: dep
+        tp: 8
+        pp: 1
+        args:
+          - '--port'
+          - '7100'
+          - '--max-num-batched-tokens'
+          - '16384'
+          - '--max-num-seqs'
+          - '3'
+          # Kept from the validated prefill lane. It disables cudagraph, so
+          # the compilation-config entry is effectively inactive on prefill.
+          - '--enforce-eager'
+          - '--additional-config'
+          - '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true}'
+        env:
+          HCCL_BUFFSIZE: '256'
+          VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1: '1'
+          VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO: '1'
+          VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ: '1'
+          VLLM_USE_V1: '1'
+          VLLM_ENGINE_ITER_TIMEOUT: '600'
+          HCCL_IF_IP: $PREFILL_NODE_1
+          HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+          GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+          TP_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+        json_args:
+          --kv-transfer-config:
+            kv_connector: MultiConnector
+            kv_role: kv_producer
+            kv_port: null
+            kv_connector_extra_config:
+              # Drop the catalog MooncakeConnectorV2 fields; this lane uses the
+              # V1 live transfer plus the Ascend store tier inside a MultiConnector.
+              prefill: null
+              decode: null
+              connectors:
+                - kv_connector: MooncakeConnectorV1
+                  kv_role: kv_producer
+                  kv_port: '30000'
+                  kv_connector_extra_config:
+                    prefill: { dp_size: 2, tp_size: 8 }
+                    decode: { dp_size: 4, tp_size: 4 }
+                - kv_connector: AscendStoreConnector
+                  kv_role: kv_producer
+                  kv_connector_extra_config:
+                    lookup_rpc_port: '0'
+                    backend: mooncake
+      decode:
+        nodes: 2
+        parallelism: dep
+        tp: 4
+        pp: 1
+        args:
+          - '--port'
+          - '7100'
+          - '--max-num-batched-tokens'
+          - '200'
+          - '--max-num-seqs'
+          - '4'
+          # The validated lane enabled the recompute scheduler on decode only.
+          - '--additional-config'
+          - '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"recompute_scheduler_enable":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true}'
+        env:
+          HCCL_BUFFSIZE: '1100'
+          VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS: '0'
+          VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO: '1'
+          VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ: '1'
+          VLLM_USE_V1: '1'
+          VLLM_ENGINE_ITER_TIMEOUT: '600'
+          HCCL_IF_IP: $DECODE_NODE_1
+          HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+          GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+          TP_SOCKET_IFNAME: $IFACE_NAME
+        json_args:
+          --kv-transfer-config:
+            kv_connector: MultiConnector
+            kv_role: kv_consumer
+            kv_port: null
+            kv_connector_extra_config:
+              prefill: null
+              decode: null
+              connectors:
+                - kv_connector: MooncakeConnectorV1
+                  kv_role: kv_consumer
+                  kv_port: '30100'
+                  kv_connector_extra_config:
+                    prefill: { dp_size: 2, tp_size: 8 }
+                    decode: { dp_size: 4, tp_size: 4 }
+                - kv_connector: AscendStoreConnector
+                  kv_role: kv_consumer
+                  kv_connector_extra_config:
+                    lookup_rpc_port: '0'
+                    backend: mooncake
+
+    runbook: |
+      ## Topology
+
+      Four Atlas 800I A2 nodes (8 x 910B4, 64 GB each):
+
+      - Prefill: two dedicated nodes, DEP with TP8 on 8 devices. Each node runs
+        one DP rank (global DP2, local DP1) on an external endpoint.
+      - Decode: two dedicated nodes, DEP with TP4 on 8 devices. Each node runs
+        two local DP ranks (global DP4, local DP2); HTTP ports are base port
+        plus the local rank, so 7100 and 7101 per node.
+      - The Ascend proxy enumerates all four decode endpoints and both prefill
+        endpoints. Do not send normal generation requests directly to a decode
+        endpoint; decode is a KV consumer and can wedge when it receives a plain
+        request.
+
+      The renderer emits external-DP worker commands for these two-node pools.
+      The validated cluster used the equivalent per-rank `vllm serve` processes
+      from `launch_online_dp.py`, with the same DP/TP sizes, rank offsets,
+      7100/7101 ports and KV connector settings.
+
+      ## Placeholders to fill
+
+      Export or replace the usual renderer variables before launch:
+      `$PREFILL_NODE_1`, `$PREFILL_NODE_2`, `$DECODE_NODE_1`, `$DECODE_NODE_2`,
+      `$PREFILL_DP_RPC_PORT`, `$DECODE_DP_RPC_PORT`, `$IFACE_NAME`,
+      `$ROUTER_HOST`, `$ROUTER_PORT`, and `$MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`.
+
+      ## Mooncake
+
+      Every prefill and decode node needs the same shared config, an exported
+      `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`, and a reachable `mooncake_master`. The validated
+      config used 15 GB per TP rank (32 clients, 480 GB total); a 1 GB value
+      only yields 32 GB and triggers eviction under two concurrent 64k requests.
+      The master ran on the first prefill node:
+
+      ```json
+      {
+        "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
+        "protocol": "ascend",
+        "device_name": "",
+        "master_server_address": "$PREFILL_NODE_1:50088",
+        "global_segment_size": "15GB",
+        "preferred_segment": false,
+        "prefer_alloc_in_same_node": true
+      }
+      ```
+
+      Start `mooncake_master --rpc_port=50088` on the first prefill node before
+      the engines. When using the rendered Docker command, add
+      `-v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf:ro` so the Ascend Mooncake backend can
+      read the host RoCE configuration; the renderer's default Ascend mount set
+      omits it.
+
+notes:
+  - title: "Use the Ascend PD preset"
+    when:
+      hardware: [ascend_910b]
+      strategies: [pd_cluster]
+      variants: [ascend_w4a8]
+    body: |
+      The supported path is the `ascend_a2_w4a8_pd` preset. It selects the Ascend proxy
+      and Mooncake (Ascend), with native external-DP workers. Baseline and other
+      routers are outside this overlay's verification scope.
+
+guide_sections:
+  ascend: |
+    ## Ascend overview
+
+    Kimi-K2.7-Code is a 1T-parameter MoE coding model with a MoonViT encoder.
+    The Ascend W4A8 checkpoint runs on Atlas 800I A2 (910B4) as a four-node
+    prefill/decode cluster: two prefill nodes with DP2 x TP8 and two decode
+    nodes with DP4 x TP4, connected through Mooncake KV transfer and fronted by
+    the Ascend proxy.
+
+    ## Ascend prerequisites
+
+    - Hardware and node topology: 4 x Atlas 800I A2, 8 x 910B4 (64 GB) each
+    - vLLM / vLLM Ascend runtime: vLLM-Ascend v0.32.0rc1
+    - Image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.32.0rc1`
+    - Checkpoint: `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K2.7-Code-w4a8` revision
+      `a671b826a7329495a89d6ff70b9c4ea96588c035`
+    - Draft: `z-lab/Kimi-K2.5-DFlash`
+    - Host: `/etc/hccn.conf` present, shared model storage mounted, one
+      `mooncake_master` reachable by every engine
+    - Both model ids resolve from ModelScope (`VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=true`)
+
+    ## Client usage
+
+    ```python
+    from openai import OpenAI
+
+    client = OpenAI(
+        base_url="http://<router-host>:<router-port>/v1",
+        api_key="EMPTY",
+    )
+    response = client.chat.completions.create(
+        model="kimi27",
+        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
+        max_tokens=1024,
+    )
+    print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+    ```
+
+    ## Ascend references
+
+    - [Kimi-K2.7-Code model card](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code)
+    - [Base recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code.yaml)
+    - [W4A8 checkpoint](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K2.7-Code-w4a8)
+    - [DFlash draft](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Kimi-K2.5-DFlash)
+    - [Ascend Mooncake PD guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html)

[Doc][BugFix] Fix invalid --random-input argument in Qwen3-Dense benchmark command (#23150)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes an invalid `--random-input` argument in the `vllm bench
serve` command within the `Qwen3-Dense.md` tutorial. The correct
argument is `--random-input-len` (see the random dataset options in vLLM

used elsewhere in this repo (e.g. `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B.md`,
`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.md`, `ucm_deployment.md`).

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No, this is a documentation-only update.

### How was this patch tested?

Verified with `markdownlint-cli2` using the repository lint
configuration (`.markdownlint.yaml`): no issues.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

[BugFix][Doc] Remove unnecessary privileged mode from Docker examples (#22622)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Remove unnecessary `--privileged` flags from Docker examples, use
explicit NPU device mappings where needed, and add Docker Engine 20.10
guidance for cgroup v2 hosts. Clarify related AI QoS and FAQ guidance.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The documented container startup commands no longer request broad

[CI][Fix] skip coverage steps when no base ref is available (#22910)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fixes #22861 

When a PR target branch does not exist locally or `github.base_ref` is
not available (e.g., PRs targeting a branch that has been deleted, or
certain workflow trigger contexts), the coverage diff steps fail with an
error because `origin/${{ github.base_ref }}` resolves to `origin/`.

This PR adds a `github.base_ref != ''` guard to all five
coverage-related steps in `_selected_tests.yaml`, so they are cleanly
skipped when no base ref is available.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. This is a CI/workflow infrastructure change only.

### How was this patch tested?
CI testing only. The change is a workflow guard condition; it will be
validated by the CI pipeline on the next PR run.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[Refactor] Drop worker overrides that duplicate upstream (#23047)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`NPUWorker` overrides a set of worker RPCs that upstream
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py::Worker` already implements with the same
behavior. I audited **every** method declared on the class against the
*effective* upstream implementation - `gpu_worker.Worker`, falling back
to `WorkerBase` where the concrete worker does not override it - on
**both** supported vLLM lanes, and deleted the ones that only restate
upstream.

Method: normalized AST comparison (`ast.dump` of each `FunctionDef`,
covering decorators, arguments, annotations, defaults and body) between
the Ascend method and the upstream method that MRO resolves to once the
override is removed, plus a second pass that compares bodies with
annotations stripped to catch annotation-only copies.

Deleted - 13 declarations, all pure delegation to upstream:

| # | method | vs v0.33.0 | vs pinned main `c410543d` | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-4 | `add_lora`, `remove_lora`, `list_loras`, `pin_lora` | identical
| identical | `return self.model_runner.<m>(...)` |
| 5-7 | `get_model`, `reset_encoder_cache`, `take_draft_token_ids` |
identical | identical | same |
| 8 | `get_supported_tasks` | body + decorators identical | same | only
a redundant quoted return annotation `"tuple[SupportedTask, ...]"`
differed |
| 9 | `reset_mm_cache` | differs (guard) | differs (guard) | upstream
calls `model_runner.reset_mm_cache()` directly; the local `getattr` +
`callable()` guard protected a runner shape that no longer exists |
| 10 | `get_draft_model` | was a `NotImplementedError` stub | same |
every supported runner implements the accessor; MRv2 returns the
speculator's draft model |
| 11-12 | `compute_weight_checksums`, `reset_weights` | differ only in
model access | same | upstream uses `model_runner.get_model()`; MRv2's
`get_model()` is literally `return self.model`, so the local
`_weight_checksum_model()` fallback was dead code |
| 13 | `_weight_checksum_model` (private helper) | Ascend-only |
Ascend-only | became unused with #11-12 |

Imports that only those methods used go away too: `LoRARequest`,
`SupportedTask`, `DraftTokenIds`, and
`compute_tensor_digests`/`zero_weights`.

**The only intended behavior change** is `get_draft_model`: the Ascend
stub used to raise `NotImplementedError`, and it now delegates to the
runner like every other worker. Everything else is byte-for-byte
equivalent, which the NPU runs below confirm. Two further notes:

- `reset_weights` no longer logs the `weight_nz_mode` advisory. The
zeroing behavior is unchanged; the NZ guard that actually rejects
unsupported usage (`_check_nz_disabled`, reached from
`_start_weight_update`) is untouched.
- The `.model`-only runner shape is no longer supported by the
weight-checker RPCs. No such runner exists: the upstream MRv2 runner
defines `get_model()` returning `self.model` on both lanes, and the v1
runner defines it too.

The same audit listed pass-through-looking methods that **do** differ on
at least one lane, so they are deliberately kept: `synchronize_device`
(`torch.npu.synchronize()`), `sample_tokens` (no `@with_gpu_sync_check`
/ `@finish_iteration_timing`), `update_config`, `reload_weights`,
`check_health`, `get_supported_pooling_tasks`, and the remaining
`NotImplementedError` stubs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No user-visible behavior change beyond removing one
`NotImplementedError` from a worker RPC that no engine path calls on
Ascend. Internal refactor; no release note fragment needed.

### How was this patch tested?

**On real NPU hardware, A/B, under both vLLM lanes** (v0.33.0 tag and
main@`c410543d`), comparing the PR against its parent commit
`7fcd50906`:

- Hardware: Ascend 910 (single die), CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu
2.10.0.post4
- vllm-ascend: `7fcd50906` (base) vs the PR head, selected via
`PYTHONPATH`
- Engine: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `enable_lora=True`, eager,
`max_model_len=512`, plus a small PEFT adapter (q_proj, r=8) generated
for the test
- `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` to reach the worker object
in-process, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` because the container's
prebuilt custom-op set predates this tree (`aclnnAddRmsNormBias`
unavailable). Both settings are applied identically to base and PR, so
the comparison is valid.

| check (same for both vLLM lanes) | base `7fcd50906` | PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compute_weight_checksums()` over 226 tensors, sha256 of all digests |
`de0b7ab0...` | `de0b7ab0...` (identical) |
| greedy generation, no LoRA | `" Paris. The capital of France is
also..."` | identical |
| greedy generation with the LoRA adapter | `" Paris, and the capital of
Italy is Rome..."` | identical |
| `add_lora` / `pin_lora` / `remove_lora` / `list_loras` | `True` /
`True` / `False` / `[]` | identical |
| `get_model`, `get_supported_tasks`, `take_draft_token_ids`,
`reset_encoder_cache`, `reset_mm_cache` |
`Qwen3ForCausalLM(151936x1024)` / `["generate"]` /
`DraftTokenIds(req_ids=[], draft_token_ids=[])` / `None` / `None` |
identical |
| `reset_weights()` -> all params zero + post-reset checksums | zeroed,
`990b038d...` | zeroed, `990b038d...` (identical) |
| `get_draft_model()` | raises `NotImplementedError` (the removed stub)
| returns `None` (runner's value) - intended |

Unit tests on the same machine, PR tree, both lanes:

- `pytest -q tests/ut/worker/test_worker_weight_checker.py
tests/ut/worker/test_worker_inheritance.py
tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py`
-
`tests/ut/worker/test_worker_inheritance.py::test_get_draft_model_reports_the_runner_drafter`
(added after review) binds the upstream runner method this RPC resolves
to and checks all three states: no speculator, a `DraftModelSpeculator`
carrying a draft module (returned by identity), and a non-draft
speculator.

Also run locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `py_compile`, and
the audit re-run -> `0 redundant`, `0 annotation-only` on both lanes.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: `get_draft_model` now covers
configured / absent / non-draft speculator; the deleted pass-throughs
add no new input domain.
- [x] **Regression test**: `test_model_accessors_are_inherited` pins
`NPUWorker.<m> is GPUWorker.<m>` for the remaining accessors, and the
new behavior test pins the one RPC whose behavior changed.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the removed
`NotImplementedError` path is exactly what the new test replaces.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: tests that asserted deleted
behavior were removed rather than weakened; A/B evidence on real NPU is
in the table above.
- [x] **Performance impact**: not applicable - no hot-path or kernel
change.

[Performance][Model] Integrate AscendC HC forward operator for Qwen4Exp (#22517)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Integrates the AscendC `TextGatedResidual` forward operator into
Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next HyperConnections on **main**, porting the
HC integration from #21794.

- Replaces the existing Triton + Linear HC mix pipeline with the fused
operator: grouped Gemma RMSNorm, down/injection projection, SiLU, up
projection and gated mixing.
- Preserves upstream checkpoint names and weight loading. Prepares the
operator's ND projection weights and FP32 norm weights once after
loading, for both the main model and MTP.
- Adds a small Triton combine kernel that consumes the operator's
**final injection weights**, avoiding a second sigmoid/channel scaling
when writing a pending block output back to the residual.

The adapter subclasses upstream `GatedResidual` and uses the existing
model-module bindings; this keeps Ascend-specific execution in the
plugin without copying the upstream model. These bindings can be
replaced by an upstream HC backend extension point when one becomes
available. No model-runner changes or new configuration switches are
introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. When the matching CANN custom operator package and Torch extension
are available, Qwen4Exp HC uses the fused path. If the package is
unavailable, or the configuration uses shared rather than per-branch HC
normalization, the upstream HC implementation remains active.

The fused path requires a CANN custom operator package that provides
`TextGatedResidual` and its matching Torch extension.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Standalone HC performance

A3 single die, BF16 input `[1,M,10240]` (`C=4`, hidden size `2560`, low
rank `320`, `eps=1e-6`, `need_backward=False`). Both implementations use
identical inputs and weights from the original `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`
checkpoint's layer-0 attention HC. This compares the complete **HC mix
stage**, rather than comparing the fused kernel against only one Triton
kernel.

NPU graph replay with NPU Event timing; initialization, compilation,
warmup and capture excluded. Two scans in opposite M orders, 22 timing
groups per implementation/M, reporting the median of per-group average
latency. Speedup = Triton / HC; lower latency is better. The two
implementations were measured in separate A3 runs; small run-to-run
differences should not be overinterpreted.

| Tokens M | Triton mix (us) | AscendC HC mix (us) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 21.97 | 25.70 | 0.855x |
| 2 | 25.25 | 26.96 | 0.937x |
| 4 | 27.85 | 27.34 | 1.019x |
| 8 | 31.45 | 28.10 | 1.119x |
| 16 | 39.15 | 28.08 | 1.394x |
| 32 | 48.13 | 34.75 | 1.385x |
| 64 | 56.49 | 41.48 | 1.362x |
| 128 | 68.85 | 52.37 | 1.315x |
| 256 | 91.09 | 64.34 | 1.416x |
| 512 | 138.96 | 106.93 | 1.299x |
| 1024 | 229.40 | 159.89 | 1.435x |
| 2048 | 425.91 | 307.33 | 1.386x |
| 4096 | 959.29 | 589.57 | 1.627x |
| 8192 | 1901.99 | 1258.79 | 1.511x |
| 16384 | 3808.97 | 2300.81 | 1.655x |
| 32768 | 7511.25 | 4187.81 | 1.794x |

Standalone output checks passed at all 16 M values in both scans, eager
and graph mode (`atol=0.02`, `rtol=0.02`). AscendC HC is faster for the
medium and large M values in this run, while M=1 and M=2 remain slower.
Separate device profiling confirmed five mix kernels on the original
path versus one `TextGatedResidual` kernel on the fused path.

#### 128K input / 1K output end-to-end performance

The measured A/B environment was fixed **vLLM `0.33.0+empty`
(`4ba787ec`) and vLLM-Ascend `main` `a41e2ff8` + #21851 `8a398c6b`**
(local merged baseline `5654ae1c`); only the HC adapter differed between
arms. This PR contains the HC port onto current main, **not the changes
from #21851**. The following results are from the pinned A/B experiment
with the `bs-boundary-20261120` package.

- A3 P/D-separated setup; each side used four cards/eight dies with DP4
x TP2 x EP8 x PP1. P always used Triton; only the D HC implementation
was ablated.
- The same pinned vLLM and vLLM-Ascend baseline, model checkpoint,
request token IDs and runtime settings were used for both arms.
- Each request had **131072 input tokens and 1024 output tokens**, with
matched fixed random token IDs, temperature 0 and `ignore_eos=true`. P
prepared the remote KV first; D timing excluded P prefill work.
- The primary capacity metric was steady D output throughput after all
streams started and before any stream completed. Each implementation
searched concurrency independently, and only completed three-round
candidates with mean request TPOT `<=20 ms` were eligible. This is the
appropriate comparison for a TPOT-constrained capacity target;
equal-concurrency results are included as diagnostics.

| Implementation | Selected concurrency | Mean TPOT (ms) | Steady output
throughput (tokens/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Triton | 31 | 16.251 | 1859.82 |
| AscendC HC | 36 | 16.027 | 1928.37 |
| HC change | - | - | **+3.69%** |

The table compares the best completed three-round candidate observed for
each implementation under the same mean-TPOT constraint. Concurrency is
searched independently because the target is maximum steady D capacity
while mean TPOT remains `<=20 ms`. The measured steady output throughput
improves by **3.69%** with AscendC HC.

#### Matching-shape `kernel_details.csv` evidence

Profiling was collected during actual 128K/1K D requests. Across 16
profiles per arm, both arms had 13,568 complete HC calls with no
unmatched or truncated calls. The matched device-kernel sums were:

| Stage | Local M | Triton (us) | AscendC HC (us) | HC change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Common combine + mix + injection | 8 | 47.42 | 38.90 | **17.96%
lower** |
| Direct mix + injection | 8 | 46.34 | 28.68 | **38.10% lower** |
| Common combine + mix + injection | 2 (D C16) | 34.23 | 33.53 | **2.05%
lower** |
| Common combine + mix + injection | 2 (D C4) | 33.88 | 34.21 | 0.96%
higher |

The Triton values are the sum of the original five-kernel chain; AscendC
values include the new combine kernel plus `TextGatedResidual`. Shapes,
rank, boundary kind and complete iterations were matched. These are
device kernel durations, not whole-request wall times, so local operator
savings do not by themselves establish an end-to-end throughput gain.

#### Integration checks

- The model-specific final-injection Triton combine is implemented in
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/qwen4_exp/hc.py` and documented in
[`qwen4_exp_hc_combine_final.md`](https://github.com/dlsccc/vllm-ascend/blob/a6159370f568beaa8fc081be776eca8ef703b526/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/qwen4_exp_hc_combine_final.md).
Its compile-time parameters are fixed by the Qwen4Exp dimensions and
injection mode; token count changes the launch grid. It has no separate
warmup registration.
- Added
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_qwen4_exp_hc_fused.py`:
**18 passed** on A3 with the pinned vLLM runtime. Covers mix
with/without injection, pending combine, zero final injection weights,
empty combine and invalid shapes/strides. Representative M values: 1, 4,
512, 1024 and 4096.
- Targeted Ruff, formatting, codespell, typos, Markdown lint,
forbidden-import, boolean-context, logger, long-function and
symbolic-meta checks passed.
- The retained benchmark artifacts include both standalone scans,
per-request E2E JSON, version/package manifests and all-rank
`kernel_details.csv` captures. The detailed benchmark artifacts are
available for review alongside the test results.
- Added `release_notes/fragments/22517.yaml` describing the A3
throughput improvement and the matching CANN operator package / Torch
extension requirement.
#### Triton specialization and recompilation validation

**White-box analysis:** This model-specific final-weight combine uses
`GROUP_DIM=2560`, `HC_COUNT=4`, `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` and the injection mode
as constexpr values. M changes the launch grid and is not a constexpr.
Tensor contents and grid changes do not require new variants; changes to
dtype, constexpr values, stride types or backend specialization classes,
source, compiler or target settings can require compilation. The
operator has no autotuning or separate warmup registration.

**Black-box validation:** A3, Triton-Ascend `3.6.0`, BF16 residual `[M,
10240]`, block output `[M, 2560]`, optional injection `[M, 4]`, with
contiguous rows. JIT calls and the compilation listener recorded shapes,
strides, pointer alignment, compiler signatures, constexpr values and
binary hashes. Process-local JIT misses, disk cache loads and native
binary compilations were counted separately.

| Directed operator validation | New binary compilations | Disk artifact
loads | New specializations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty-cache first calls, both injection modes | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Two M sweeps after those first calls | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 10 graph captures and 50 replays | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Each of two fresh processes, same disk cache, first calls | 0 | 2 | 0
|
| Each fresh-process sweep, capture and replay phase | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The sweeps covered `M = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024,
2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768` in ascending and descending order, with
both injection modes. Graph capture covered `M = 1, 4, 32, 1024, 8192`
in both modes, with five replays each. Every output matched the FP32
Torch reference followed by the BF16 store exactly (`atol=0`, `rtol=0`).
The two binary hashes corresponded to `HAS_INJECTION=False/True`;
pointer signatures were `*bf16`, row-stride signatures were `i32`,
pointers were 16-byte aligned, and runtime specialization attributes
were empty. M changes added no variants in these runs.

The same production kernel and adapter were observed in the pinned
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next A3 service (`TP8`, EP, MTP3, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`),
using the vLLM/vLLM-Ascend runtime identified above. Executed source
SHA256 values matched PR revision
`25b9290a224711c2cf2eae49056b567aa747a02c`. One serial request completed
with verified input/output token counts of 131072/1024.

| Model-service phase | JIT misses | New binary compilations | Disk
artifact loads | Observed M |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Startup, all 8 workers | 8 | 8 | 0 | 1, 2, 4, 1024 |
| Completed 128K/1K request | 0 | 0 | 0 | 64, 960, 1024 |

Startup produced the same single binary hash independently in each
worker: eight process-local compilations, one unique specialization.
Serving calls and graph replay reused that hash. Observed serving M
values describe JIT launches; captured graph replay can execute kernels
without invoking the Python JIT entry point. These compilation counts
apply to the tested dimensions, dtype, layout and toolchain; they are
separate from the throughput benchmark above.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM-Ascend project
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm_ascend.models.qwen4_exp.hc_fused import AscendTextGatedResidual
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.qwen4_exp.hc import combine_final
+
+pytest.importorskip("cann_ops_transformer.ops.mhc.text_gated_residual.text_gated_residual")
+
+
+def make_hc(use_combine, hc_per_branch_norm=True):
+    # Exercise the checkpoint-facing weight preparation without distributed
+    # Linear initialization; the operator consumes these ordinary ND tensors.
+    module = AscendTextGatedResidual.__new__(AscendTextGatedResidual)
+    nn.Module.__init__(module)
+    module.config = SimpleNamespace(hc_lowrank=320, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, hc_per_branch_norm=hc_per_branch_norm)
+    module.hc_count = 4
+    module.hidden_size = 2560
+    module.use_combine = use_combine
+    module._textgr_enabled = hc_per_branch_norm
+    for name in ("_textgr_gamma", "_textgr_down", "_textgr_up", "_textgr_gate"):
+        module.register_buffer(name, None, persistent=False)
+    module.hc_norm = nn.Linear(10240, 1, bias=False, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="npu")
+    module.hc_norm.weight.data = torch.randn(10240, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1
+    down = nn.Linear(10240, 336 if use_combine else 320, bias=False, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="npu")
+    if use_combine:
+        module.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject = down
+    else:
+        module.input_mix_weight_down = down
+    module.input_mix_weight_up = nn.Linear(320, 10240, bias=False, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="npu")
+    module.prepare_textgr_weights()
+    return module
+
+
+def reference_mix(module, x):
+    groups = x.float().reshape(-1, 4, 2560)
+    norm = groups * torch.rsqrt(groups.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + module.config.rms_norm_eps)
+    norm = (norm.flatten(1) * (1 + module.hc_norm.weight.float())).to(x.dtype)
+    lowrank = F.linear(norm, module._textgr_down)
+    lowrank = F.silu(lowrank.float() / 4).to(x.dtype)
+    gates = F.linear(lowrank, module._textgr_up)
+    mixed = (norm.float() * gates.float().sigmoid()).reshape(-1, 4, 2560).mean(1).to(x.dtype)
+    injection = None
+    if module.use_combine:
+        injection = (2 * torch.sigmoid(F.linear(norm, module._textgr_gate).float() / 4)).to(x.dtype)
+    return mixed, injection
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 4, 512, 1024, 4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_combine", [False, True])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_mix_and_pending_combine(tokens, use_combine):
+    torch.manual_seed(21794)
+    module = make_hc(use_combine)
+    x = torch.randn(tokens, 10240, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    expected, expected_injection = reference_mix(module, x)
+    residual, mixed, injection = module.mix(x)
+    assert residual is x
+    torch.testing.assert_close(mixed, expected, atol=0.02, rtol=0.02)
+    if use_combine:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(injection, expected_injection, atol=0.02, rtol=0.02)
+    else:
+        assert injection is None
+
+    block = torch.randn(tokens, 2560, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    final_injection = torch.rand(tokens, 4, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 2
+    combined = x.float().reshape(-1, 4, 2560) + block.float()[:, None] * final_injection.float()[:, :, None]
+    combined = combined.flatten(1).to(x.dtype)
+    actual_residual, actual_mixed, _ = module.combine_and_mix(x, block, final_injection)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_residual, combined, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_mixed, reference_mix(module, combined)[0], atol=0.02, rtol=0.02)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [0, 1, 7])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_injection", [False, True])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_combine_uses_final_weights(tokens, with_injection):
+    x = torch.randn(tokens, 10240, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    block = torch.randn(tokens, 2560, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    # Zero weights distinguish final weights from logits (sigmoid(0) != 0).
+    injection = torch.zeros(tokens, 4, device="npu", dtype=x.dtype) if with_injection else None
+    expected = x if with_injection else (x.float().reshape(-1, 4, 2560) + block.float()[:, None]).flatten(1).to(x.dtype)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(combine_final(x, block, injection, 4), expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+def test_shared_hc_norm_uses_upstream_implementation():
+    module = make_hc(True, hc_per_branch_norm=False)
+    module.prepare_textgr_weights()
+    assert module._textgr_enabled is False
+    assert module._textgr_gamma is None
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_reject_incompatible_inputs():
+    module = make_hc(True)
+    x = torch.zeros(1, 10240, device="npu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    block = torch.zeros(1, 2560, device="npu", dtype=x.dtype)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="model input"):
+        module.mix(x.unsqueeze(0))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="block output"):
+        combine_final(x, block[:, :-1], None, 4)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="final injection"):
+        combine_final(x, block, torch.zeros(1, 3, device="npu"), 4)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="divisible"):
+        combine_final(torch.zeros(1, 10242, device="npu"), block, None, 4)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="inner strides"):
+        combine_final(x, block, torch.zeros(1, 8, device="npu")[:, ::2], 4)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="inner strides"):
+        combine_final(torch.zeros(1, 20480, device="npu")[:, ::2], block, None, 4)
+    cpu_residual = torch.zeros(1, 10240)
+    cpu_block = torch.ones(1, 2560)
+    expected = cpu_residual.reshape(1, 4, 2560) + cpu_block[:, None]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(combine_final(cpu_residual, cpu_block, None, 4), expected.flatten(1))
